\section{Introduction to Pandas
Fundamentals}\label{introduction-to-pandas-fundamentals}

In the \textbf{Reading Data} chapter, we learned how to load data files
into pandas DataFrames. Now we'll dive deeper into pandas' powerful
capabilities for data manipulation and analysis.

Pandas is an essential tool in the data scientist or data analyst's
toolkit due to its ability to handle and transform data with ease and
efficiency.

\subsection{Pandas in the Data Science
Ecosystem}\label{pandas-in-the-data-science-ecosystem}

Pandas doesn't work in isolation - it's designed to integrate seamlessly
with other Python libraries:

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2143}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.5714}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2143}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Library
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Integration with Pandas
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Purpose
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{NumPy} & Built on NumPy arrays & Mathematical operations and
array processing \\
\textbf{Matplotlib} & Direct plotting from DataFrames & Data
visualization and charts \\
\textbf{Seaborn} & Native DataFrame support & Statistical
visualizations \\
\textbf{Scikit-learn} & Seamless data flow & Machine learning
algorithms \\
\textbf{SciPy} & Statistical analysis & Advanced statistical
functions \\
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Core Pandas Capabilities}\label{core-pandas-capabilities}

Throughout this chapter, you'll master these essential pandas
operations:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Creating Series \& DataFrames}: From Python data structures\\
\item
  \textbf{Filtering \& Subsetting}: Extract exactly the data you need\\
\item
  \textbf{Sorting \& Ranking}: Organize data for analysis\\
\item
  \textbf{Adding \& Removing}: Modify DataFrame structure\\
\item
  \textbf{Data Types}: Work with different types of data
\end{itemize}

\begin{quote}
💡 \textbf{Learning Path}: We'll start with fundamental concepts and
progressively build toward advanced data manipulation techniques, giving
you a complete toolkit for real-world data analysis.
\end{quote}

Now let's start by importing the essential Pandas library:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ pandas }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ pd}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\section{Creating Pandas Series \&
DataFrames}\label{creating-pandas-series-dataframes}

There are \textbf{two primary approaches} for creating pandas data
structures, each serving different purposes in your data analysis
workflow:

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method 1: Reading from External Data
Sources}}{Method 1: Reading from External Data Sources}}\label{method-1-reading-from-external-data-sources}

In real-world data science, you'll typically work with data stored in
external files or databases. This is the most common approach for
production analysis.

\textbf{Popular Data Sources:}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.4103}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2564}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Source Type
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Pandas Function
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Use Case
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{CSV Files} & \texttt{pd.read\_csv()} & Most common - structured
tabular data \\
\textbf{Excel Files} & \texttt{pd.read\_excel()} & Business data,
reports with multiple sheets \\
\textbf{JSON Files} & \texttt{pd.read\_json()} & API data, web services,
nested data \\
\textbf{SQL Databases} & \texttt{pd.read\_sql()} & Enterprise databases,
large datasets \\
\textbf{HTML Tables} & \texttt{pd.read\_html()} & Web scraping, online
data tables \\
\end{longtable}

\begin{quote}
💡 \textbf{Pro Tip}: We covered these methods extensively in the
\textbf{Reading Data} chapter. If you need a refresher on loading
external data, refer back to that section!
\end{quote}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method 2: Creating from Python Data
Structures}}{Method 2: Creating from Python Data Structures}}\label{method-2-creating-from-python-data-structures}

When you need to create data programmatically or work with small
datasets for testing and learning, you can build DataFrames and Series
directly from Python objects.

\textbf{Benefits of this approach:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Testing \& Learning}: Perfect for experimenting with pandas
  features
\item
  \textbf{Data Generation}: Create synthetic data for analysis
\item
  \textbf{Small Datasets}: Handle simple, manual data entry
\item
  \textbf{Prototyping}: Quick data structure creation for
  proof-of-concepts
\end{itemize}

Let's explore how to create pandas data structures from scratch!

\subsubsection{Creating Series from Python Data
Structures}\label{creating-series-from-python-data-structures}

A \textbf{Series} is pandas' 1D data structure - think of it as a smart,
labeled list or array.

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method A: From a Python
List}}{Method A: From a Python List}}\label{method-a-from-a-python-list}

The simplest way to create a Series is from a Python list. Pandas
automatically assigns integer indices starting from 0.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#Defining a Pandas Series}
\NormalTok{series\_example }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.Series([}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}these\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}are\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}english\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}words\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{series\_example}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
0      these
1        are
2    english
3      words
dtype: object
\end{verbatim}

\textbf{🔍 Key Observation}: Notice the automatic integer indices (0, 1,
2, 3) on the left!

\textbf{Custom Indexing}: You can provide meaningful labels instead of
default numbers using the \texttt{index} parameter:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#Defining a Pandas Series with custom row labels}
\NormalTok{series\_example }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.Series([}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}these\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}are\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}english\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}words\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], index }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{101}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{105}\NormalTok{))}
\NormalTok{series\_example}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
101      these
102        are
103    english
104      words
dtype: object
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method B: From a Python
Dictionary}}{Method B: From a Python Dictionary}}\label{method-b-from-a-python-dictionary}

Dictionaries are perfect for creating Series with \textbf{meaningful
labels}. The dictionary keys automatically become the Series index, and
values become the data points.

\textbf{Perfect for}: Time series data, named categories, any key-value
relationships

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📊 Real{-}world example: US GDP per capita by year (1960{-}2021)}
\CommentTok{\# Notice some years are missing {-} pandas handles this gracefully!}
\NormalTok{GDP\_per\_capita\_dict }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1960\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{3007}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1961\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{3067}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1962\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{3244}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1963\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{3375}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1964\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{3574}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1965\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{3828}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1966\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{4146}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1967\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{4336}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1968\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{4696}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1970\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{5234}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1971\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{5609}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1972\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{6094}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1973\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{6726}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1974\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{7226}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1975\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{7801}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1976\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{8592}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1978\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{10565}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1979\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{11674}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1980\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{12575}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1981\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{13976}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1982\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{14434}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1983\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{15544}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1984\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{17121}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1985\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{18237}\NormalTok{,  }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1986\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{19071}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1987\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{20039}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1988\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{21417}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1989\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{22857}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1990\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{23889}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1991\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{24342}\NormalTok{,  }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1992\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{25419}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1993\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{26387}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1994\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{27695}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1995\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{28691}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1996\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{29968}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1997\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{31459}\NormalTok{,  }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1998\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{32854}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2000\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{36330}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2001\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{37134}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2002\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{37998}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2003\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{39490}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2004\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{41725}\NormalTok{,  }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2005\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{44123}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2006\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{46302}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2007\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{48050}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2008\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{48570}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2009\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{47195}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2010\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{48651}\NormalTok{,  }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2011\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{50066}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2012\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{51784}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2013\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{53291}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2015\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{56763}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2016\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{57867}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2017\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{59915}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2018\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{62805}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2019\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{65095}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2020\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{63028}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2021\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{69288}\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#Example 2: Creating a Pandas Series from a Dictionary}
\NormalTok{GDP\_per\_capita\_series }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.Series(GDP\_per\_capita\_dict)}
\NormalTok{GDP\_per\_capita\_series.head()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
1960    3007
1961    3067
1962    3244
1963    3375
1964    3574
dtype: int64
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Creating a DataFrame from Python Data
Structures}\label{creating-a-dataframe-from-python-data-structures}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method A: From a list of Python
Dictionary}}{Method A: From a list of Python Dictionary}}\label{method-a-from-a-list-of-python-dictionary}

You can create a DataFrame where keys are column names and values are
lists representing column data.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#List of dictionary consisting of 52 playing cards of the deck}
\NormalTok{deck\_list\_of\_dictionaries }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [\{}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}value\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:i, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}suit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:c\}}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ c }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}spades\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}clubs\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}hearts\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}diamonds\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{15}\NormalTok{)]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#Example 3: Creating a Pandas DataFrame from a List of dictionaries}
\NormalTok{deck\_df }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(deck\_list\_of\_dictionaries)}
\NormalTok{deck\_df.head()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
& value & suit \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
0 & 2 & spades \\
1 & 3 & spades \\
2 & 4 & spades \\
3 & 5 & spades \\
4 & 6 & spades \\
\end{longtable}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method B: From a Python
Dictionary}}{Method B: From a Python Dictionary}}\label{method-b-from-a-python-dictionary-1}

You can create a DataFrame where keys are column names and values are
lists representing column data.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#Example 4: Creating a Pandas DataFrame from a Dictionary}
\NormalTok{dict\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{],}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}B\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{],}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}C\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{200}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{300}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{400}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{500}\NormalTok{]\}}

\NormalTok{dict\_df }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(dict\_data)}
\NormalTok{dict\_df}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
& A & B & C \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
0 & 1 & 20 & 100 \\
1 & 2 & 10 & 200 \\
2 & 3 & 50 & 300 \\
3 & 4 & 40 & 400 \\
4 & 5 & 30 & 500 \\
\end{longtable}

\section{Data Selection and
Filtering}\label{data-selection-and-filtering}

Now that you understand series and dataframe are two foundamental data
structures in pandas, let's master the art of \textbf{extracting exactly
the data you need}. Data selection and filtering are fundamental skills
that you'll use in every pandas project.

\subsection{Basic Selection}\label{basic-selection}

\subsubsection{Extracting Column(s)}\label{extracting-columns}

The first step when working with a DataFrame is often to extract one or
more columns. To do this effectively, it's helpful to understand the
internal structure of a DataFrame. Conceptually, you can think of a
DataFrame as a dictionary of lists, where the keys are column names, and
the values are lists or arrays containing data for the respective
columns.

\textbf{Loading Our Practice Dataset}

Let's work with a real movie ratings dataset to practice our selection
techniques:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ pandas }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ pd}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.read\_csv(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./datasets/movie\_ratings.csv\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings.head()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}llllllllllll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
& Title & US Gross & Worldwide Gross & Production Budget & Release Date
& MPAA Rating & Source & Major Genre & Creative Type & IMDB Rating &
IMDB Votes \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
0 & Opal Dreams & 14443 & 14443 & 9000000 & Nov 22 2006 & PG/PG-13 &
Adapted screenplay & Drama & Fiction & 6.5 & 468 \\
1 & Major Dundee & 14873 & 14873 & 3800000 & Apr 07 1965 & PG/PG-13 &
Adapted screenplay & Western/Musical & Fiction & 6.7 & 2588 \\
2 & The Informers & 315000 & 315000 & 18000000 & Apr 24 2009 & R &
Adapted screenplay & Horror/Thriller & Fiction & 5.2 & 7595 \\
3 & Buffalo Soldiers & 353743 & 353743 & 15000000 & Jul 25 2003 & R &
Adapted screenplay & Comedy & Fiction & 6.9 & 13510 \\
4 & The Last Sin Eater & 388390 & 388390 & 2200000 & Feb 09 2007 &
PG/PG-13 & Adapted screenplay & Drama & Fiction & 5.7 & 1012 \\
\end{longtable}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method 1: Single Column
Extraction}}{Method 1: Single Column Extraction}}\label{method-1-single-column-extraction}

Each column represents a \textbf{feature} of your data. There are
\textbf{two ways} to extract a single column:

\textbf{A) Bracket Notation:
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}column\_name\textquotesingle{}{]}}}
(Recommended)

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  ✅ Always works\\
\item
  ✅ Handles column names with spaces
\item
  ✅ Clear and explicit
\end{itemize}

\textbf{B) Dot Notation: \texttt{df.column\_name}} (Limited use)

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  ❌ Fails with spaces in column names
\item
  ❌ Conflicts with DataFrame methods
\item
  ✅ Shorter syntax for simple names
\end{itemize}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings.Title}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
0                         Opal Dreams
1                        Major Dundee
2                       The Informers
3                    Buffalo Soldiers
4                  The Last Sin Eater
                    ...              
2223                      King Arthur
2224                            Mulan
2225                       Robin Hood
2226    Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves
2227                       Spiceworld
Name: Title, Length: 2228, dtype: object
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🧠 Understanding the DataFrame structure: }
\CommentTok{\# DataFrames work like dictionaries with enhanced features!}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings\_dict }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:  [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Opal Dreams\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Major Dundee\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}The Informers\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Buffalo Soldiers\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}The Last Sin Eater\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}US Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{:  [}\DecValTok{14443}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{14873}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{315000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{353743}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{388390}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{14443}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{14873}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{315000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{353743}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{388390}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Production Budget\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{9000000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3800000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{18000000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{15000000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2200000}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\textbf{Dictionary Analogy:}

Just like accessing dictionary values by key:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings\_dict[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
['Opal Dreams',
 'Major Dundee',
 'The Informers',
 'Buffalo Soldiers',
 'The Last Sin Eater']
\end{verbatim}

\textbf{DataFrame Column Extraction:}

Similarly, we extract DataFrame columns by column name:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
0                         Opal Dreams
1                        Major Dundee
2                       The Informers
3                    Buffalo Soldiers
4                  The Last Sin Eater
                    ...              
2223                      King Arthur
2224                            Mulan
2225                       Robin Hood
2226    Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves
2227                       Spiceworld
Name: Title, Length: 2228, dtype: object
\end{verbatim}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method 2: Multiple Column
Selection}}{Method 2: Multiple Column Selection}}\label{method-2-multiple-column-selection}

\textbf{Key Rule}: Use a \textbf{list of column names} inside the
brackets:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Single column → Series}
\NormalTok{df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}column\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]        }

\CommentTok{\# Multiple columns → DataFrame  }
\NormalTok{df[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}col1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}col2\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\textbf{🔍 Notice}: Double brackets \texttt{{[}{[}{]}{]}} create a list,
which tells pandas you want multiple columns!

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}US Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ ]]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsubsection{Extracting Row(s)}\label{extracting-rows}

In many cases, we need to filter rows based on specific conditions or a
combination of multiple conditions. Next, let's explore how to use these
conditions effectively to extract rows that meet our criteria, whether
it's a single condition or multiple conditions combined

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Single Condition
Filtering}}{Single Condition Filtering}}\label{single-condition-filtering}

Filter rows in a DataFrame based on \textbf{one logical condition}.\\
This is the most common way to extract a subset of data, such as
selecting all rows where a column's values meet a specific criterion
(e.g., greater than, equal to, not equal).

For Example:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# extracting the rows that have IMDB Rating greater than 8}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Multiple Conditions
Filtering}}{Multiple Conditions Filtering}}\label{multiple-conditions-filtering}

When filtering with more than one condition, use \textbf{logical
operators}:

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3571}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3214}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3214}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Operator
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Purpose
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Example
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{\&} & \textbf{AND} -- both conditions must be True &
\texttt{(df{[}\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \textgreater{}\ 5)\ \&\ (df{[}\textquotesingle{}B\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \textless{}\ 10)} \\
\texttt{\textbackslash{}\textbar{}} & \textbf{OR} -- at least one
condition must be True &
\texttt{(df{[}\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \textgreater{}\ 5)\ \textbackslash{}\textbar{}\ (df{[}\textquotesingle{}B\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \textless{}\ 10)} \\
\texttt{\textasciitilde{}} & \textbf{NOT} -- negates the condition &
\texttt{\textasciitilde{}(df{[}\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \textgreater{}\ 5)} \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{🚨 Important Rule:} Always wrap each condition in
\textbf{parentheses} \texttt{()} to avoid operator precedence errors.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# extracting the rows that have IMDB Rating greater than 8 and US Gross less than 1000000}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}US Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{1000000}\NormalTok{)]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Negating Conditions with the
\texttt{\textasciitilde{}}
Operator}}{Negating Conditions with the \textasciitilde{} Operator}}\label{negating-conditions-with-the-operator}

The tilde (\texttt{\textasciitilde{}}) operator in pandas is used to
\textbf{negate boolean conditions}, making it especially useful when you
want to \emph{exclude} certain rows.

Instead of selecting rows that satisfy a condition,
\texttt{\textasciitilde{}} allows you to filter rows that \textbf{do
not} meet that condition. This is helpful for refining queries and
focusing on the remaining data.

For example, if you want all rows where \texttt{IMDB\ Rating} is
\emph{not} equal to \texttt{8}, you can write:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Excluding the rows that have IMDB Rating that equals 8 using the tilde \textasciitilde{}}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\OperatorTok{\textasciitilde{}}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{)]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Advanced Selection: \texttt{.loc{[}{]}} and
\texttt{.iloc{[}{]}}}{Advanced Selection: .loc{[}{]} and .iloc{[}{]}}}\label{advanced-selection-.loc-and-.iloc}

When you need \textbf{precise control} over both rows and columns,
pandas provides two powerful indexers that let you select exactly what
you need.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{\texttt{.loc{[}{]}} vs
\texttt{.iloc{[}{]}}: The Key
Difference}}{.loc{[}{]} vs .iloc{[}{]}: The Key Difference}}\label{loc-vs-.iloc-the-key-difference}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2647}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1765}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2941}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2647}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Indexer
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Uses
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Best For
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Example
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{\texttt{.loc{[}{]}}} & \textbf{Labels} (names) & Human-readable
selection &
\texttt{df.loc{[}\textquotesingle{}row\_name\textquotesingle{},\ \textquotesingle{}column\_name\textquotesingle{}{]}} \\
\textbf{\texttt{.iloc{[}{]}}} & \textbf{Positions} (numbers) &
Programmatic selection & \texttt{df.iloc{[}0,\ 1{]}} \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Mental Model}

Think of your DataFrame like a \textbf{spreadsheet}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{.loc{[}{]}}} works like clicking on \textbf{named}
  rows/columns (A1, B2, etc.)
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{.iloc{[}{]}}} works like clicking on \textbf{position}
  numbers (row 0, column 1, etc.)
\end{itemize}

\begin{quote}
💡 \textbf{Memory Tip}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{loc}} = \textbf{L}abels/\textbf{L}ocation names
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{iloc}} = \textbf{i}nteger \textbf{loc}ations
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Using \texttt{.loc{[}{]}} -
Label-Based
Selection}}{Using .loc{[}{]} - Label-Based Selection}}\label{using-.loc---label-based-selection}

\textbf{Syntax}: \texttt{df.loc{[}row\_indexer,\ column\_indexer{]}}

\textbf{Key Features:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Uses \textbf{actual labels} (index names, column names)
\item
  \textbf{Inclusive} of both endpoints in slicing
\item
  Can combine with boolean conditions
\item
  Most \textbf{intuitive} for data analysis
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Example}: Let's subset the \texttt{Title},
\texttt{Worldwide\ Gross}, \texttt{Production\ Budget}, and
\texttt{IMDB\ Rating} of the top 3 movies using specific row indices
that obtained from the above sorting table.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📍 Select specific rows by index and specific columns by name}
\NormalTok{movies\_subset }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings\_sorted.loc[[}\DecValTok{182}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2084}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{790}\NormalTok{], [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}US Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Production Budget\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🎬 Selected movies with key financial and rating data:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{movies\_subset}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\end{verbatim}

Budget \\

790 & Schindler\textquotesingle s List & 8.9 & 96067179 & 321200000 &

\end{longtable}

The \texttt{:} symbol in \texttt{.loc} is a slicing operator that
represents a range or all elements in the specified dimension (rows or
columns). Use \texttt{:} alone to select all rows/columns, or with
start/end points to slice specific parts of the DataFrame.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📊 Select ALL rows (:) but only specific columns}
\NormalTok{movies\_subset }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings\_sorted.loc[:, [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Production Budget\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{" All movies with financial and rating columns only:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{movies\_subset}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Combining \texttt{.loc} with
Boolean
Conditions}}{Combining .loc with Boolean Conditions}}\label{combining-.loc-with-boolean-conditions}

\textbf{Power Move}: Filter rows AND select columns simultaneously using
boolean logic!

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# extracting the rows that have IMDB Rating greater than 8 or US Gross less than 1000000, only extract the Title and IMDB Rating columns}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}US Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{1000000}\NormalTok{)][[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}

\CommentTok{\#using loc to extract the rows that have IMDB Rating greater than 8 or US Gross less than 1000000, only extract the Title and IMDB Rating columns}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings.loc[(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}US Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{1000000}\NormalTok{),[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Using \texttt{.iloc{[}{]}} -
Position-Based
Selection}}{Using .iloc{[}{]} - Position-Based Selection}}\label{using-.iloc---position-based-selection}

\textbf{Syntax}:
\texttt{df.iloc{[}row\_positions,\ column\_positions{]}}

\textbf{Key Features:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Uses \textbf{integer positions} (0-based indexing like Python lists)
\item
  \textbf{Exclusive} of end point in slicing (like Python slicing)
\item
  Great for \textbf{systematic sampling} or \textbf{first/last N
  records}
\item
  Think: ``\textbf{i}nteger \textbf{loc}ation''
\end{itemize}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Position Type & Example & Description \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Single} & \texttt{df.iloc{[}0,\ 1{]}} & First row, second
column \\
\textbf{List} & \texttt{df.iloc{[}{[}0,\ 2{]},\ {[}1,\ 3{]}{]}} &
Specific positions \\
\textbf{Slice} & \texttt{df.iloc{[}0:3,\ 1:4{]}} & Range (exclusive
end) \\
\textbf{All} & \texttt{df.iloc{[}:,\ :{]}} & All rows and columns \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{💡 Memory Tip}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  iloc = \textbf{i}nteger positions,
\item
  loc = \textbf{l}abel names
\end{itemize}

🤔 \textbf{Critical Thinking Question}: Can you use \texttt{.iloc} for
conditional filtering (like
\texttt{df.iloc{[}df{[}\textquotesingle{}column\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \textgreater{}\ 5{]}})?

\textbf{Answer}: ❌ \textbf{No!} \texttt{.iloc} only accepts
\textbf{integer positions}, not boolean conditions. For conditional
filtering, you must use \texttt{.loc} or boolean indexing directly.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Summary: \texttt{.loc} vs
\texttt{.iloc} - Choose Your
Weapon!}}{Summary: .loc vs .iloc - Choose Your Weapon!}}\label{summary-.loc-vs-.iloc---choose-your-weapon}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1636}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3818}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.4545}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Feature
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
\texttt{.loc} (Label-Based)
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
\texttt{.iloc} (Position-Based)
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Uses} & 🏷️ \textbf{Labels/Names} & 🔢 \textbf{Integer
Positions} \\
\textbf{Slicing} & \texttt{{[}start:end{]}} \textbf{includes} end &
\texttt{{[}start:end{]}} \textbf{excludes} end \\
\textbf{Examples} &
\texttt{df.loc{[}\textquotesingle{}row\_name\textquotesingle{},\ \textquotesingle{}col\_name\textquotesingle{}{]}}
& \texttt{df.iloc{[}0,\ 1{]}} \\
\textbf{Conditions} & ✅
\texttt{df.loc{[}df{[}\textquotesingle{}col\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \textgreater{}\ 5{]}}
& ❌ No boolean conditions \\
\textbf{Best For} & \textbf{Business logic} filtering &
\textbf{Systematic} sampling \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Mental Model}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{.loc} = ``Give me the data \textbf{by name/label}''
\item
  \texttt{.iloc} = ``Give me the data \textbf{by position number}''
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Finding Extremes in pandas: Values, Labels, and
Positions}\label{finding-extremes-in-pandas-values-labels-and-positions}

\subsubsection{Finding extreme values}\label{finding-extreme-values}

When you need to find extreme values, pandas offers powerful methods:

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Method & Purpose & Returns \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{min()} & 📉 \textbf{Actual minimum} value & The minimum value
itself \\
\texttt{max()} & 📈 \textbf{Actual maximum} value & The maximum value
itself \\
\end{longtable}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# find the max/min worldwide gross}
\NormalTok{max\_gross }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{"Worldwide Gross"}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{min\_gross }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{min}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{"Worldwide Gross"}\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Hignest gross:"}\NormalTok{, max\_gross)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Minimum gross:"}\NormalTok{, min\_gross)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Hignest gross: 2767891499
Minimum gross: 884
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Finding extreme labels}\label{finding-extreme-labels}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1566}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.4217}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2892}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1325}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Method
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Purpose
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Returns
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Use With
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{idxmax()} & 🏷️ \textbf{Label} of maximum & Index label &
\texttt{.loc} \\
\texttt{idxmin()} & 🏷️ \textbf{Label} of minimum & Index label &
\texttt{.loc} \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{💡 Pro Tip}: Use \texttt{idx} methods to \textbf{locate} the
extreme values, then use \texttt{.loc} to get the full row!

\textbf{\texttt{min()} / \texttt{max()} vs.~\texttt{idxmin()} /
\texttt{idxmax()}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Use \textbf{\texttt{min()} / \texttt{max()}} when you only need the
  \textbf{extreme value} itself.\\
\item
  Use \textbf{\texttt{idxmin()} / \texttt{idxmax()}} when you need to
  know \textbf{where that extreme occurs} --- i.e., the \textbf{index
  label}, so you can fetch the corresponding row.
\end{itemize}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Find the INDEX LABELS of movies with max/min worldwide gross}
\NormalTok{max\_gross\_index }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings\_sorted[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].idxmax()}
\NormalTok{min\_gross\_index }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings\_sorted[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].idxmin()}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🏆 Highest grossing movie index:"}\NormalTok{, max\_gross\_index)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📉 Lowest grossing movie index:"}\NormalTok{, min\_gross\_index)}

\CommentTok{\# 🔍 Now get the full details of these movies}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{ Highest grossing movie:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings\_sorted.loc[max\_gross\_index, [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{ Lowest grossing movie:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings\_sorted.loc[min\_gross\_index, [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]])}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
🏆 Highest grossing movie index: 2094
📉 Lowest grossing movie index: 896

 Highest grossing movie:
Title                  Avatar
Worldwide Gross    2767891499
Name: 2094, dtype: object

 Lowest grossing movie:
Title              In Her Line of Fire
Worldwide Gross                    884
Name: 896, dtype: object
\end{verbatim}

\textbf{Workflow}: \texttt{idxmin()}/\texttt{idxmax()} return
\textbf{index labels} → use with \texttt{.loc} to extract full rows

\textbf{Example}: Find the index, then get the actual value:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 💰 Get the actual gross values using the indices we found}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{" Max worldwide gross:"}\NormalTok{, }\SpecialStringTok{f"$}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings\_sorted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{loc[max\_gross\_index, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{" Min worldwide gross:"}\NormalTok{, }\SpecialStringTok{f"$}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings\_sorted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{loc[min\_gross\_index, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
 Max worldwide gross: $2,767,891,499
 Min worldwide gross: $884
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Finding extreme
positions}\label{finding-extreme-positions}

When you need \textbf{position numbers} instead of \textbf{label names},
you need to use \texttt{argmax()} and \texttt{argmin()}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2162}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2432}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2432}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2973}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Method
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Purpose
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Returns
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Use With
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{argmax()} & 📍 \textbf{Position} of maximum & Integer index
(0-based) & \texttt{.iloc} \\
\texttt{argmin()} & 📍 \textbf{Position} of minimum & Integer index
(0-based) & \texttt{.iloc} \\
\end{longtable}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Find POSITIONS (not labels) of movies with max/min worldwide gross  }
\NormalTok{max\_position }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings\_sorted[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].argmax()}
\NormalTok{min\_position }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings\_sorted[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].argmin()}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🏆 Max gross at position:"}\NormalTok{, max\_position)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📉 Min gross at position:"}\NormalTok{, min\_position)}

\CommentTok{\# 🔍 Use iloc with positions to get the actual values}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{💰 Max worldwide gross:"}\NormalTok{, }\SpecialStringTok{f"$}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings\_sorted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{iloc[max\_position, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"💸 Min worldwide gross:"}\NormalTok{, }\SpecialStringTok{f"$}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings\_sorted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{iloc[min\_position, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🎬 Get full movie details using positions}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🎭 Movies with extreme gross values:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Highest:"}\NormalTok{, movie\_ratings\_sorted.iloc[max\_position][}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Lowest:"}\NormalTok{, movie\_ratings\_sorted.iloc[min\_position][}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
🏆 Max gross at position: 48
📉 Min gross at position: 2149

💰 Max worldwide gross: $2,767,891,499
💸 Min worldwide gross: $884

🎭 Movies with extreme gross values:
Highest: Avatar
Lowest: In Her Line of Fire
\end{verbatim}

\textbf{Pro Tips for Min/Max Operations}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2632}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.5000}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2368}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Scenario
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Recommended Method
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Reason
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Custom/Non-unique indices} & \texttt{idxmax()} /
\texttt{idxmin()} & Returns meaningful labels \\
\textbf{Simple position-based work} & \texttt{argmax()} /
\texttt{argmin()} & Direct integer positions \\
\textbf{Find max/min across rows} & \texttt{df.idxmax(axis=1)} & Column
name with max value per row \\
\textbf{Find max/min across columns} & \texttt{df.idxmax(axis=0)} & Row
index with max value per column \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{🧠 Memory Aid}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{idx} → \textbf{labels} → use with \texttt{.loc}
\item
  \texttt{arg} → \textbf{positions} → use with \texttt{.iloc}
\end{itemize}

\section{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Sorting \& Ranking}: Organize data for
analysis}{Sorting \& Ranking: Organize data for analysis}}\label{sorting-ranking-organize-data-for-analysis}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Why Sorting and Ranking
Matter}}{Why Sorting and Ranking Matter}}\label{why-sorting-and-ranking-matter}

Sorting and ranking are fundamental operations in data analysis that
help you:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Identify top performers} (best movies, highest sales)
\item
  \textbf{Understand distributions} (from lowest to highest values)
\item
  \textbf{Find outliers} (extreme values at the ends)
\item
  \textbf{Create ordered presentations} (leaderboards, reports)
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Basic Sorting with
\texttt{sort\_values()}}}{Basic Sorting with sort\_values()}}\label{basic-sorting-with-sort_values}

\textbf{Syntax}:
\texttt{df.sort\_values(by=\textquotesingle{}column\_name\textquotesingle{},\ ascending=True/False)}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Parameter & Purpose & Options \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{by} & Column(s) to sort by & Single column or list of columns \\
\texttt{ascending} & Sort direction & \texttt{True} (low→high),
\texttt{False} (high→low) \\
\texttt{na\_position} & Where to put NaN values &
\texttt{\textquotesingle{}first\textquotesingle{}} or
\texttt{\textquotesingle{}last\textquotesingle{}} \\
\texttt{inplace} & Modify original DataFrame & \texttt{True} or
\texttt{False} \\
\end{longtable}

\begin{Shaded}

\CommentTok{\# 🎬 Sort movies by IMDB Rating (ascending {-} lowest to highest)}
\NormalTok{movies\_by\_rating\_asc }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.sort\_values(by}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, ascending}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{True}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔥 Movies sorted by IMDB Rating (worst to best):"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🏆 Sort movies by IMDB Rating (descending {-} highest to lowest)  }
\NormalTok{movies\_by\_rating\_desc }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.sort\_values(by}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, ascending}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🌟 Movies sorted by IMDB Rating (best to worst):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movies\_by\_rating\_desc[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head())}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Ranking Methods with
\texttt{rank()}}}{Ranking Methods with rank()}}\label{ranking-methods-with-rank}

\textbf{Purpose}: Assign numerical ranks to values (1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.)

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Method & Handling Ties & Example (values: {[}1, 2, 2, 4{]}) \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{\textquotesingle{}average\textquotesingle{}} & Average of tied
ranks & {[}1.0, 2.5, 2.5, 4.0{]} \\
\texttt{\textquotesingle{}min\textquotesingle{}} & Minimum rank for ties
& {[}1, 2, 2, 4{]} \\
\texttt{\textquotesingle{}max\textquotesingle{}} & Maximum rank for ties
& {[}1, 3, 3, 4{]} \\
\texttt{\textquotesingle{}first\textquotesingle{}} & Order of appearance
& {[}1, 2, 3, 4{]} \\
\texttt{\textquotesingle{}dense\textquotesingle{}} & No gaps in ranks &
{[}1, 2, 2, 3{]} \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{💡 Use Cases}: Create leaderboards, percentile rankings,
performance tiers

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🏆 Create rankings for IMDB ratings (higher rating = better rank)}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Rank\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].rank(ascending}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{, method}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}min\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 💰 Create rankings for worldwide gross (higher gross = better rank)  }
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Rank\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].rank(ascending}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{, method}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}min\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Show top 10 movies by IMDB rating with their ranks}
\NormalTok{top\_rated }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.nsmallest(}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Rank\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🌟 Top 10 Movies by IMDB Rating:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(top\_rated[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Rank\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Rank\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].to\_string(index}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{))}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 💎 Compare: Movies that are highly rated vs highly grossing}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🎭 Rating vs Gross Performance Analysis:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{comparison }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Rank\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Rank\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head(}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(comparison.to\_string(index}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Percentile Ranking}\label{percentile-ranking}

Percentile ranking allows you to convert raw ranks into
\textbf{percentiles (0--100\%)}, giving a clearer sense of each value's
\textbf{relative position} in the dataset.\\
This is especially useful when comparing across datasets of different
sizes or when you want a normalized measure of ranking.

In pandas, you can compute percentile ranks using the \texttt{rank()}
method with the parameter \texttt{pct=True}:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📊 Calculate percentile rankings (0{-}100\%)}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].rank(pct}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{True}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{100}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].rank(pct}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{True}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{100}

\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Interpret percentiles}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📈 Percentile Interpretation Guide:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• 90th+ percentile = Top 10\% (Excellent)"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• 75th+ percentile = Top 25\% (Very Good)"}\NormalTok{)  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• 50th+ percentile = Above Average"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Below 50th = Below Average"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🏆 Top performers in both rating AND gross:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{top\_both }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}
\NormalTok{    (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{90}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&} 
\NormalTok{    (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{90}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{][[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}

\ControlFlowTok{if} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(top\_both) }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{:}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(top\_both.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{).to\_string(index}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{))}
\ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{:}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🤔 No movies in top 10}\SpecialCharTok{\% f}\StringTok{or both rating AND gross!"}\NormalTok{)}
    
\CommentTok{\# 🎭 Show some examples with percentile context}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📊 Sample movies with percentile context:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{sample }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Percentile\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(sample.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{).to\_string(index}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Advanced Sorting
Techniques}\label{advanced-sorting-techniques}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{Custom Sorting with
\texttt{sort\_values(key=function)}}{Custom Sorting with sort\_values(key=function)}}\label{custom-sorting-with-sort_valueskeyfunction}

The \texttt{key} parameter in \texttt{sort\_values()} lets you apply a
\textbf{transformation function} to column values \textbf{before
sorting}.\\
This is useful when the natural order of values is not the same as the
order you want to sort by.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎬 Custom sorting: Sort movie titles by length (shortest to longest)}
\NormalTok{movies\_by\_title\_length }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.sort\_values(}
\NormalTok{    by}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }
\NormalTok{    key}\OperatorTok{=}\KeywordTok{lambda}\NormalTok{ x: x.}\BuiltInTok{str}\NormalTok{.}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{()  }\CommentTok{\# Sort by title length, not alphabetically}
\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📏 Movies sorted by title length (shortest to longest):"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{title\_length\_sample }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movies\_by\_title\_length[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head(}\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ title\_length\_sample.iterrows():}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"📖 \textquotesingle{}}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{\textquotesingle{} (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ chars) {-} ⭐ }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🎭 Sort by absolute deviation from average rating (find most "average" movies)}
\NormalTok{avg\_rating }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].mean()}
\NormalTok{movies\_by\_avg\_deviation }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.sort\_values(}
\NormalTok{    by}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
\NormalTok{    key}\OperatorTok{=}\KeywordTok{lambda}\NormalTok{ x: }\BuiltInTok{abs}\NormalTok{(x }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ avg\_rating)  }\CommentTok{\# Sort by distance from average}
\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📊 Movies closest to average rating (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{avg\_rating}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{):"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{avg\_movies }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movies\_by\_avg\_deviation[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ avg\_movies.iterrows():}
\NormalTok{    deviation }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{abs}\NormalTok{(row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ avg\_rating)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"🎯 \textquotesingle{}}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{\textquotesingle{} {-} Rating: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (±}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{deviation}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ from avg)"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{Index Sorting with
\texttt{sort\_index()}}{Index Sorting with sort\_index()}}\label{index-sorting-with-sort_index}

Sort DataFrame by \textbf{row indices} or \textbf{column names} rather
than values

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📋 First, let\textquotesingle{}s see the current index order}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔍 Current index range:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"First 5 indices: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings.index[:}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{])}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Last 5 indices: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings.index[}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{:])}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🔄 Sort by index in ascending order (restore original row order)}
\NormalTok{movies\_index\_sorted }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.sort\_index()}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📊 After sorting by index (ascending):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"First 5 indices: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movies\_index\_sorted.index[:}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{])}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🔽 Sort by index in descending order}
\NormalTok{movies\_index\_desc }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.sort\_index(ascending}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📊 After sorting by index (descending):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"First 5 indices: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movies\_index\_desc.index[:}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{])}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🏷️ Sort columns alphabetically by column names}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📝 Original column order:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Columns: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings.columns)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{movies\_cols\_sorted }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.sort\_index(axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# axis=1 for columns}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔤 Columns after alphabetical sorting:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Columns: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movies\_cols\_sorted.columns)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Top-N and Bottom-N
Selection}\label{top-n-and-bottom-n-selection}

When you want the \textbf{largest or smallest N values} in a Series or
DataFrame, pandas provides efficient methods that avoid a full sort:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{nlargest(n)}} → returns the top \texttt{n} rows with
  the highest values\\
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{nsmallest(n)}} → returns the bottom \texttt{n} rows
  with the lowest values
\end{itemize}

These are \textbf{faster than sorting} the entire DataFrame with
\texttt{.sort\_values()}, especially for large datasets.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🏆 Top 5 highest{-}grossing movies (using nlargest)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"💰 Top 5 Highest{-}Grossing Movies:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{top\_gross }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.nlargest(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ top\_gross.iterrows():}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"💎 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} $}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (⭐ }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🌟 Top 5 highest{-}rated movies (using nlargest)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{⭐ Top 5 Highest{-}Rated Movies:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{top\_rated }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.nlargest(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ top\_rated.iterrows():}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"🎭 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} ⭐ }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ ($}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📉 Bottom 5 lowest{-}rated movies (using nsmallest)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{💀 Bottom 5 Lowest{-}Rated Movies:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{bottom\_rated }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.nsmallest(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ bottom\_rated.iterrows():}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"😬 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} ⭐ }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ ($}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 💸 Bottom 5 lowest{-}grossing movies (using nsmallest)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{💸 Bottom 5 Lowest{-}Grossing Movies:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{bottom\_gross }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.nsmallest(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ bottom\_gross.iterrows():}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"📉 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} $}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (⭐ }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\texttt{sort\_values()} & \textbf{Full sorting} & Slower for large data
& Complete ranking, detailed analysis \\
\texttt{nlargest(n)} & \textbf{Top N only} & ⚡ \textbf{Faster} for
small N & Leaderboards, top performers \\
\texttt{nsmallest(n)} & \textbf{Bottom N only} & ⚡ \textbf{Faster} for
small N & Finding outliers, worst performers \\

competition rankings \\

\textbf{💡 Pro Tip}: Use \texttt{nlargest()}/\texttt{nsmallest()} when
you only need the top/bottom few records!

\subsection{Real-World Sorting
Scenarios}\label{real-world-sorting-scenarios}

Let's apply sorting and ranking to solve common business questions:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎬 Scenario 1: Find "Hidden Gems" {-} High rating but low gross}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"💎 HIDDEN GEMS: Great movies that didn\textquotesingle{}t make much money"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{55}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Create efficiency ratio: Rating per dollar (higher = better value)}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Rating\_per\_Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{/} \DecValTok{1\_000\_000}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{hidden\_gems }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}
\NormalTok{    (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \FloatTok{7.5}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&} 
\NormalTok{    (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].median())}
\NormalTok{].nlargest(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ hidden\_gems.iterrows():}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"🎭 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   ⭐ Rating: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ | 💰 Gross: $}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{55}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Scenario 2: Find "Blockbuster Hits" {-} High gross AND high rating  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🚀 BLOCKBUSTER HITS: Great movies that made tons of money"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{55}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{blockbusters }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}
\NormalTok{    (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \FloatTok{7.0}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&} 
\NormalTok{    (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].quantile(}\FloatTok{0.8}\NormalTok{))}
\NormalTok{].sort\_values([}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], ascending}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{[}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{, }\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{]).head(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{)}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ blockbusters.iterrows():}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"🏆 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   ⭐ Rating: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ | 💰 Gross: $}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{55}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📊 Scenario 3: ROI Analysis {-} Best return on investment}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🎯 ROI CHAMPIONS: Best gross{-}to{-}budget ratio"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{55}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Calculate ROI ratio (avoid division by zero)}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ROI\_Ratio\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Production Budget\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].replace(}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{top\_roi }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.nlargest(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ROI\_Ratio\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ idx, row }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ top\_roi.iterrows():}
\NormalTok{    roi }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ROI\_Ratio\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"💰 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   📈 ROI: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{roi}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{x | Budget: $}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Production Budget\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ → Gross: $}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{row[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:,.0f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}
