\subsection{*Key Takeaways: Sorting \& Ranking
Mastery**}\label{key-takeaways-sorting-ranking-mastery}

\textbf{Essential Methods}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{sort\_values()}}: Complete sorting by column values
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{rank()}}: Assign numerical ranks (1st, 2nd, 3rd\ldots)
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{nlargest()} / \texttt{nsmallest()}}: Efficient
  top/bottom N selection\\
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{sort\_index()}}: Sort by row indices or column names
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Decision Framework}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Quick reference for method selection}
\ControlFlowTok{if} \StringTok{"I need top/bottom N only"}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{    use\_nlargest\_or\_nsmallest()}
\ControlFlowTok{elif} \StringTok{"I need complete ordering"}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{    use\_sort\_values()  }
\ControlFlowTok{elif} \StringTok{"I need relative positions"}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{    use\_rank()}
\ControlFlowTok{elif} \StringTok{"I need custom ordering logic"}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{    use\_sort\_values\_with\_key\_function()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\textbf{💡 Pro Tips}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Performance}: \texttt{nlargest(5)} beats
  \texttt{sort\_values().head(5)} for large datasets
\item
  \textbf{Multiple columns}:
  \texttt{sort\_values({[}\textquotesingle{}col1\textquotesingle{},\ \textquotesingle{}col2\textquotesingle{}{]},\ ascending={[}True,\ False{]})}
\item
  \textbf{Percentiles}: \texttt{rank(pct=True)\ *\ 100} for 0-100\%
  percentile scores
\item
  \textbf{Custom logic}: Use \texttt{key=lambda\ x:\ transform(x)} for
  complex sorting rules
\item
  \textbf{Stability}: pandas sorting is \textbf{stable} (preserves
  original order for ties)
\end{enumerate}

\emph{🎬 Next up: Learn how to add and remove your sorted data!}

\section{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Adding \& Removing}: Modify DataFrame
structure}{Adding \& Removing: Modify DataFrame structure}}\label{adding-removing-modify-dataframe-structure}

\subsection{Why DataFrame Structure Modification
Matters}\label{why-dataframe-structure-modification-matters}

Real-world data analysis often requires:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Adding new columns} (calculated fields, derived metrics)
\item
  \textbf{Removing columns} (irrelevant features, memory optimization)
\item
  \textbf{Removing rows} (outliers, invalid data, filtering)
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Adding Columns to
DataFrames}\label{adding-columns-to-dataframes}

There are multiple ways to add new columns, each with different use
cases:

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method 1: Direct
Assignment}}{Method 1: Direct Assignment}}\label{method-1-direct-assignment}

The simplest way to add a column with a constant value or calculated
field. The added column will be put at the end of the dataframe

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎬 Let\textquotesingle{}s work with our movie dataset to demonstrate column operations}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Original DataFrame shape:"}\NormalTok{, movie\_ratings.shape)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Original columns:"}\NormalTok{, }\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings.columns))}

\CommentTok{\# 💡 Method 1a: Add a constant value column}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Data\_Source\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB\textquotesingle{}}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{✅ Added constant column \textquotesingle{}Data\_Source\textquotesingle{}"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 💡 Method 1b: Add calculated column based on existing data}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Production Budget\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"✅ Added calculated column \textquotesingle{}Profit\textquotesingle{}"}\NormalTok{)}


\CommentTok{\# 📈 Show results}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🎯 New DataFrame shape:"}\NormalTok{, movie\_ratings.shape)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🆕 Sample of new columns:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Data\_Source\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

✅ Added constant column 'Data_Source'
✅ Added calculated column 'Profit'

🎯 New DataFrame shape: (2228, 19)

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Method 3: Using \texttt{insert()}
for Specific
Positioning}}{Method 3: Using insert() for Specific Positioning}}\label{method-3-using-insert-for-specific-positioning}

When you need to \textbf{control exactly where} the new column appears

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{movies\_copy[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
0       Nov 22 2006
1       Apr 07 1965
2       Apr 24 2009
3       Jul 25 2003
4       Feb 09 2007
           ...     
2223    Jul 07 2004
2224    Jun 19 1998
2225    May 14 2010
2226    Jun 14 1991
2227    Jan 23 1998
Name: Release Date, Length: 2228, dtype: object
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Method 3: insert() for precise column positioning}
\CommentTok{\# Create a working copy to demonstrate insert()}
\NormalTok{movies\_copy }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.copy()}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📋 Original column order (first 5):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movies\_copy.columns[:}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{]))}

\CommentTok{\# 📍 Insert a column at position 2 (after Title and Genre)}
\CommentTok{\# 1) Parse the date column (e.g., "Nov 22 2006")}
\NormalTok{movies\_copy[}\StringTok{"Release Date"}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.to\_datetime(movies\_copy[}\StringTok{"Release Date"}\NormalTok{], }\BuiltInTok{format}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{"\%b }\SpecialCharTok{\%d}\StringTok{ \%Y"}\NormalTok{, errors}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{"coerce"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{movies\_copy.insert(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Decade\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, (movies\_copy[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].dt.year }\OperatorTok{//} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📍 Insert another column at the beginning (position 0)  }
\NormalTok{movies\_copy.insert(}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Movie\_ID\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_copy) }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{))}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{ New column order (first 6):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movies\_copy.columns[:}\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{]))}


\CommentTok{\# ⚠️ Note: insert() modifies the DataFrame in{-}place}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{ DataFrame shape after inserts: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movies\_copy}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{ Sample with positioned columns:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{movies\_copy[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Movie\_ID\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Major Genre\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Decade\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Removing Columns from
DataFrames}\label{removing-columns-from-dataframes}

The most common and flexible way to remove columns is with
\textbf{\texttt{.drop()}}.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  By default, \texttt{.drop()} works on \textbf{rows}, so you need to
  specify \texttt{axis=1} (or \texttt{columns=}) to drop columns.\\
\item
  You can remove \textbf{one column} or \textbf{multiple columns} at the
  same time.\\
\item
  \texttt{.drop()} returns a \textbf{new DataFrame} unless you use
  \texttt{inplace=True}.
\end{itemize}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🗂️ Setup: Create a working copy with extra columns for deletion demo}
\NormalTok{movies\_for\_deletion }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.copy()}

\CommentTok{\# Add some temporary columns to demonstrate deletion}
\NormalTok{movies\_for\_deletion[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Temp\_Col1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Delete\_Me\textquotesingle{}}
\NormalTok{movies\_for\_deletion[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Temp\_Col2\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_for\_deletion))}
\NormalTok{movies\_for\_deletion[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Temp\_Col3\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movies\_for\_deletion[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{2}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📋 DataFrame before deletion:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movies\_for\_deletion}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Columns: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(movies\_for\_deletion.columns)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Using drop() {-} most common and flexible}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{ Using drop()"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Drop single column}
\NormalTok{movies\_method1 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movies\_for\_deletion.drop(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Temp\_Col1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After dropping 1 column: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movies\_method1}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Drop multiple columns}
\NormalTok{movies\_method1b }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movies\_for\_deletion.drop([}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Temp\_Col1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Temp\_Col2\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After dropping 2 columns: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movies\_method1b}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}


\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📊 Final comparison {-} all methods result in same shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movies\_method1b}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
📋 DataFrame before deletion:
Shape: (2228, 22)
Columns: ['Title', 'US Gross', 'Worldwide Gross', 'Production Budget', 'Release Date', 'MPAA Rating', 'Source', 'Major Genre', 'Creative Type', 'IMDB Rating', 'IMDB Votes', 'Rating_Rank', 'Gross_Rank', 'Rating_Percentile', 'Gross_Percentile', 'Rating_per_Gross', 'ROI_Ratio', 'Data_Source', 'Profit', 'Temp_Col1', 'Temp_Col2', 'Temp_Col3']

 Using drop()
After dropping 1 column: (2228, 21)
After dropping 2 columns: (2228, 20)

📊 Final comparison - all methods result in same shape: (2228, 20)
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Removing Rows from
DataFrames}\label{removing-rows-from-dataframes}

There are several ways to remove or filter out unwanted rows in a
DataFrame:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  using \texttt{drop()}
\item
  boolean filtering
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{Method 1: Using
\texttt{.drop()}}{Method 1: Using .drop()}}\label{method-1-using-.drop}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Works by specifying the \textbf{row index labels} to remove.\\
\item
  Returns a new DataFrame unless you use \texttt{inplace=True}.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Method2: Boolean
Filtering}\label{method2-boolean-filtering}

\begin{itemize}
\item
  Keep only rows that meet a condition (the most common method in data
  analysis).
\item
  More flexible than \texttt{drop()}, especially when conditions depend
  on column values.
\end{itemize}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎬 Row removal demonstrations}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 Original dataset info:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Total movies: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"IMDB Rating range: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{min}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# ❌ Method 1: Remove rows by index using drop()}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔧 Method 1: Remove specific rows by index"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{movies\_drop\_index }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.drop([}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{])  }\CommentTok{\# Remove first 3 movies}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After dropping first 3 rows: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_drop\_index)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# ❌ Method 2: Remove rows by condition (Boolean filtering)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔧 Method 2: Remove rows by condition"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Remove movies with low ratings (\textless{} 5.0)}
\NormalTok{movies\_no\_low\_rating }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IMDB Rating\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \FloatTok{5.0}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{removed\_count }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings) }\OperatorTok{{-}} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_no\_low\_rating)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Removed }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{removed\_count}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies with rating \textless{} 5.0"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Remaining: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_no\_low\_rating)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Remove movies with missing/zero gross}
\NormalTok{movies\_with\_gross }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Worldwide Gross\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{removed\_no\_gross }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings) }\OperatorTok{{-}} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_with\_gross) }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Removed }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{removed\_no\_gross}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies with no gross data"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Remaining: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_with\_gross)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies"}\NormalTok{)}


\CommentTok{\# 📊 Summary of filtering effects}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📈 Filtering Summary:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original dataset: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After rating filter: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_no\_low\_rating)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_no\_low\_rating)}\OperatorTok{/}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings)}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{100}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{\%)"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After gross filter: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_with\_gross)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ movies (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movies\_with\_gross)}\OperatorTok{/}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings)}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{100}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{\%)"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
📊 Original dataset info:
Total movies: 2228
IMDB Rating range: 1.4 - 9.2

🔧 Method 1: Remove specific rows by index
After dropping first 3 rows: 2225 movies

🔧 Method 2: Remove rows by condition
Removed 324 movies with rating < 5.0
Remaining: 1904 movies
Removed 0 movies with no gross data
Remaining: 2228 movies

📈 Filtering Summary:
Original dataset: 2228 movies
After rating filter: 1904 movies (85.5%)
After gross filter: 2228 movies (100.0%)
\end{verbatim}

\section{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Data Types}: Working with Different
Data
Formats}{Data Types: Working with Different Data Formats}}\label{data-types-working-with-different-data-formats}

\subsection{Why Data Types Matter in Data
Science}\label{why-data-types-matter-in-data-science}

Data types are \textbf{fundamental} to pandas operations:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Functionality}: Type-specific methods (\texttt{.str},
  \texttt{.dt} accessors)
\item
  \textbf{Speed}: Vectorized operations work best with proper types
\item
  \textbf{Data Integrity}: Prevent incorrect calculations and
  comparisons
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Complete Pandas Data Types
Reference}\label{complete-pandas-data-types-reference}

\subsection{Data Type Detection and
Inspection}\label{data-type-detection-and-inspection}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🔍 Comprehensive data type exploration}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{" DATA TYPE ANALYSIS"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📊 Basic data type information}

\subsection{Data Type Conversion}\label{data-type-conversion}

Often, after the inital reading, we need to convert the datatypes of
some of the columns to make them suitable for analysis,as the available
functions and operations depend on the column's data type. For example,
the datatype of Release Date in the DataFrame \texttt{movie\_ratings} is
object. To perform datetime related computations on this variable, we'll
need to convert it to a datatime format. We'll use the Pandas function
\texttt{to\_datatime()} to covert it to a datatime format. Similar
functions such as \texttt{to\_numeric()}, \texttt{to\_string()} etc.,
can be used for other conversions.

In Pandas, the
\texttt{errors=\textquotesingle{}coerce\textquotesingle{}} parameter is
often used in the context of data conversion, specifically when using
the \texttt{pd.to\_numeric} function. This argument tells Pandas to
convert values that it can and set the ones it cannot convert to
\texttt{NaN}. It's a way of gracefully handling errors without raising
an exception. Read the textbook for an example

\subsubsection{Core Conversion
Functions}\label{core-conversion-functions}

\textbf{\texttt{pd.to\_numeric()}} & String → Number &

\textbf{\texttt{pd.to\_datetime()}} & String → DateTime &
\texttt{errors=\textquotesingle{}coerce\textquotesingle{}} &

\texttt{datetime} \\

\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}col\textquotesingle{}{]}.astype(\textquotesingle{}int\textquotesingle{})} \\

categorical data \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{💡 Pro Tip}:
\texttt{errors=\textquotesingle{}coerce\textquotesingle{}} converts
invalid values to \texttt{NaN} instead of throwing errors!

Next, we'll convert the \texttt{Release\ Date} column in the DataFrame
to the \texttt{datetime} format to facilitate further analysis.

\subsubsection{Comprehensive Type Conversion
Examples}\label{comprehensive-type-conversion-examples}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎯 COMPREHENSIVE TYPE CONVERSION EXAMPLES}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔄 TYPE CONVERSION DEMONSTRATIONS"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📅 1. DateTime Conversion (Year → Full Date)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📅 1. DateTime Conversion:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Before: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{dtype}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Convert years to datetime (assuming January 1st)}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.to\_datetime(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], }\BuiltInTok{format}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}mixed\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{dtype}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Sample converted values:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].head())}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🔢 2. Numeric Conversion Example}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔢 2. Numeric Conversion with Error Handling:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Create sample data with mixed types for demonstration}
\NormalTok{sample\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.Series([}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}100\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}200.5\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}invalid\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}300\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\VariableTok{None}\NormalTok{])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original data: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{sample\_data}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{tolist()}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Safe conversion with error handling}
\NormalTok{numeric\_converted }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.to\_numeric(sample\_data, errors}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}coerce\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After to\_numeric(): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{numeric\_converted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{tolist()}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Data type: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{numeric\_converted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{dtype}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)}


\CommentTok{\# 🔧 3. Custom astype() Conversions}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔧 3. Custom Type Conversions with astype():"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Create sample numeric data}
\NormalTok{sample\_numeric }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.Series([}\FloatTok{1.7}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{2.3}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{3.9}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{4.1}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{5.8}\NormalTok{])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original (float): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{sample\_numeric}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{tolist()}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Convert float to int (truncates decimals)}
\NormalTok{int\_converted }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sample\_numeric.astype(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}int\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"As integer: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{int\_converted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{tolist()}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Convert to string}
\NormalTok{str\_converted }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sample\_numeric.astype(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}string\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"As string: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{str\_converted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{tolist()}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"String dtype: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{str\_converted}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{dtype}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

datetime methods} for temporal analysis and feature engineering.

\subsubsection{📈 Practical DateTime Feature
Engineering}\label{practical-datetime-feature-engineering}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📅 COMPREHENSIVE DATETIME FEATURE ENGINEERING}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📅 DATETIME FEATURE EXTRACTION"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🗓️ 1. Extract multiple date components}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Year\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].dt.year}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Month\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].dt.month  }
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Quarter\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].dt.quarter}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Weekday\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].dt.weekday}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_DayName\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].dt.day\_name()}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_MonthName\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].dt.month\_name()}

\CommentTok{\# 📊 Display extracted features}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 Extracted DateTime Features:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{datetime\_features }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release Date\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Year\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Month\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Quarter\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_DayName\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[datetime\_features].head())}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📈 2. Create business{-}relevant features}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📈 Business{-}Relevant DateTime Features:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Decade classification}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Decade\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Year\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{//} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{10}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🎬 Movies by Decade:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Decade\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].value\_counts().sort\_index())}

\CommentTok{\# Era classification}
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Era\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Year\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].}\BuiltInTok{apply}\NormalTok{(}
    \KeywordTok{lambda}\NormalTok{ x: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Silent Era\textquotesingle{}} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{1930} \ControlFlowTok{else}
              \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Golden Age\textquotesingle{}} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{1960} \ControlFlowTok{else}  
              \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}New Hollywood\textquotesingle{}} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{1980} \ControlFlowTok{else}
              \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Modern Era\textquotesingle{}} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{2000} \ControlFlowTok{else}
              \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Digital Era\textquotesingle{}}
\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🎭 Movies by Era:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Era\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].value\_counts())}

\CommentTok{\# Season classification  }
\NormalTok{movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Season\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Month\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].}\BuiltInTok{apply}\NormalTok{(}
    \KeywordTok{lambda}\NormalTok{ x: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Winter\textquotesingle{}} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ x }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{] }\ControlFlowTok{else}
              \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Spring\textquotesingle{}} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ x }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{] }\ControlFlowTok{else}
              \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Summer\textquotesingle{}} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ x }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{] }\ControlFlowTok{else}
              \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Fall\textquotesingle{}}
\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🌱 Movies by Release Season:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Season\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].value\_counts())}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📋 Sample with All Features:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{feature\_cols }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Title\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Year\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Decade\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Era\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_Season\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Release\_DayName\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(movie\_ratings[feature\_cols].head())}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Working with \texttt{object}
Data}{Working with object Data}}\label{working-with-object-data}

In pandas, the \texttt{object} data type is a flexible data type that
can store a mix of text (strings), mixed types, or arbitrary Python
objects. It is commonly used for string data and is a key part of
working with categorical or unstructured data in pandas.

Similar to datetime objects having a \texttt{dt} accessor, a number of
specialized string methods are available when using the \texttt{str}
accessor. These methods have in general matching names with the
equivalent built-in string methods for single elements, but are applied
element-wise on each of the values of the columns.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{the \texttt{str} accessor in
pandas}{the str accessor in pandas}}\label{the-str-accessor-in-pandas}

The \texttt{str} accessor in pandas provides a wide range of string
methods that allow for efficient and convenient text processing on an
entire Series of strings. Here are some commonly used str methods:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  String splitting: \texttt{str.split()}
\item
  String joining: \texttt{str.join()}
\item
  Substrings: \texttt{str.slice(start,\ stop)}, \texttt{str{[}0{]}}
\item
  String Case Conversion: \texttt{str.lower()}, \texttt{str.upper()},
  \texttt{str.capitalize()}
\item
  Whitespace Removal: \texttt{str.strip()}, \texttt{str.lstrip()},
  \texttt{str.rstrip()}
\item
  Replacing and Removing:
  \texttt{str.replace(\textquotesingle{}old\textquotesingle{},\ \textquotesingle{}new\textquotesingle{})}
\item
  Pattern matching and extraction:
  \texttt{str.contains(\textquotesingle{}pattern\textquotesingle{})},
  \texttt{startswith(\textquotesingle{}prefix\textquotesingle{})},
  \texttt{endswith(\textquotesingle{}suffix\textquotesingle{})}
\item
  String length and counting: \texttt{str.len()}, \texttt{str.count()}
\end{itemize}

Let's use the well-known titanic dataset to illustrate how to manipulate
string columns in pandas dataframe next

\begin{Shaded}

\NormalTok{titanic.head()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The \texttt{Name} column varies in length and contains passengers' last
names, titles, and first names. By extracting the title from the
\texttt{Name} column, we could infer the \textbf{sex} of the passenger
and add it as a new feature. This could potentially be a significant
predictor of survival, as the ``ladies first'' principle was often
applied during the Titanic evacuation. Adding this feature may enhance
the model's ability to predict whether a passenger survived.

\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🔍 Comprehensive analysis of numerical data}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔢 NUMERICAL DATA ANALYSIS OVERVIEW"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Display basic info about our dataset}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📊 Dataset Overview:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Numerical columns: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{movie\_ratings}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{select\_dtypes(include}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}number\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{columns}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{tolist()}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Enhanced describe() with interpretation}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📈 COMPREHENSIVE STATISTICAL SUMMARY:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{desc\_stats }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.describe()}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(desc\_stats)}

\CommentTok{\# Interpret the results}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{💡 Key Insights from describe():"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{)}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ col }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ movie\_ratings.select\_dtypes(include}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}number\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]).columns:}
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ col }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ desc\_stats.columns:}
\NormalTok{        mean\_val }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ desc\_stats.loc[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}mean\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, col]}
\NormalTok{        median\_val }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ desc\_stats.loc[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}50\%\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, col]}
\NormalTok{        std\_val }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ desc\_stats.loc[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}std\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, col]}
        
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🎯 }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{col}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{:"}\NormalTok{)}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   • Average: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{mean\_val}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   • Median: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{median\_val}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   • Spread (Std): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{std\_val}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

        \CommentTok{\# Interpret skewness (very rough heuristic using mean vs. median)}
        \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ pd.notna(mean\_val) }\KeywordTok{and}\NormalTok{ pd.notna(median\_val) }\KeywordTok{and}\NormalTok{ pd.notna(std\_val) }\KeywordTok{and}\NormalTok{ std\_val }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{            skew\_direction }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{"right"} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ mean\_val }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ median\_val }\ControlFlowTok{else} \StringTok{"left"}
            \ControlFlowTok{if} \BuiltInTok{abs}\NormalTok{(mean\_val }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ median\_val) }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \FloatTok{0.1} \OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ std\_val:}
                \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   • Distribution: Skewed }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{skew\_direction}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
            \ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{:}
                \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"   • Distribution: Roughly symmetric"}\NormalTok{)}
        \ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{:}
            \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"   • Distribution: Not assessed (insufficient variation or NaNs)"}\NormalTok{)    }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Individual Statistical
Methods}\label{individual-statistical-methods}

Beyond \texttt{describe()}, pandas offers \textbf{granular statistical
methods} for specific analysis needs:

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Method & Purpose & Business Example \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{mean()} & Average value & Average customer age, mean sales \\
\texttt{median()} & Middle value & Median income, typical order size \\
\texttt{mode()} & Most frequent & Most common product rating \\
\texttt{std()} & Standard deviation & Risk assessment, quality
control \\
\texttt{var()} & Variance & Data volatility, consistency \\
\texttt{min()} / \texttt{max()} & Range bounds & Performance
benchmarks \\
\texttt{quantile()} & Percentiles & Customer segments, outlier
detection \\
\texttt{sum()} & Total & Revenue totals, inventory counts \\
\texttt{count()} & Non-null values & Data completeness \\
\end{longtable}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{Summary Statistics: Rows vs Columns with
\texttt{axis}
Parameter}{Summary Statistics: Rows vs Columns with axis Parameter}}\label{summary-statistics-rows-vs-columns-with-axis-parameter}

\textbf{Critical Concept}: The \texttt{axis} parameter controls the
\textbf{direction} of calculation: - \textbf{\texttt{axis=0}} (default):
Calculate \textbf{down} the rows (column-wise aggregation) -
\textbf{\texttt{axis=1}}: Calculate \textbf{across} the columns
(row-wise aggregation)

\textbf{💡 Memory Trick}: - \texttt{axis=0} → ``\textbf{0} rows away'' →
Column results - \texttt{axis=1} → ``\textbf{1} column away'' → Row
results

\section{\texorpdfstring{Understanding \texttt{inplace=True} vs
\texttt{inplace=False}}{Understanding inplace=True vs inplace=False}}\label{understanding-inplacetrue-vs-inplacefalse}

\subsection{Why This Matters: Memory, Performance, and
Safety}\label{why-this-matters-memory-performance-and-safety}

The \texttt{inplace} parameter is one of the \textbf{most important
concepts} in pandas for:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Memory management} (avoid unnecessary copies)
\item
  \textbf{Data integrity} (prevent accidental modifications)
\item
  \textbf{Performance optimization} (reduce overhead)
\item
  \textbf{Debugging} (track data transformations)
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Core Concept: Modify vs
Create}\label{core-concept-modify-vs-create}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 10\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1618}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 10\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1471}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 10\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1176}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 10\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2206}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 10\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2059}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 10\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1471}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Parameter
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Behavior
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Memory
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Original Data
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Return Value
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Use Case
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{\texttt{inplace=False}} & 🆕 \textbf{Creates new copy} & 📈
Higher usage & ✅ \textbf{Unchanged} & Modified DataFrame & \textbf{Safe
exploration} \\
\textbf{\texttt{inplace=True}} & 🔄 \textbf{Modifies original} & 📉
Lower usage & ❌ \textbf{Changed permanently} & \texttt{None} &
\textbf{Final transformations} \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{🚨 Critical Rule}: \texttt{inplace=True} returns \texttt{None},
not the modified DataFrame!

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Comprehensive inplace demonstration}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔄 INPLACE PARAMETER DEMONSTRATION"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📊 Create sample business data}
\NormalTok{original\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(\{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Employee\_ID\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{101}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{102}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{103}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{104}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{105}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Name\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Alice\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Bob\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Charlie\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Diana\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Eva\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Department\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IT\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}HR\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IT\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Finance\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}HR\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Salary\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{75000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{65000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{80000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{70000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{68000}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Years\_Experience\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{\})}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📋 Original DataFrame:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(original\_data)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"📍 DataFrame ID: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{id}\NormalTok{(original\_data)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# Memory address}

\CommentTok{\# 🆕 Method 1: inplace=False (DEFAULT)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔧 Method 1: inplace=False (Creates New Copy)"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Add bonus column without modifying original}
\NormalTok{df\_with\_bonus }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ original\_data.assign(Bonus}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{original\_data[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Salary\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*} \FloatTok{0.1}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"✅ New DataFrame with bonus:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(df\_with\_bonus[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Name\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Salary\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Bonus\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{))}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"📍 New DataFrame ID: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{id}\NormalTok{(df\_with\_bonus)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔍 Original DataFrame (unchanged):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(original\_data.head(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{))}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"📍 Original ID still: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{id}\NormalTok{(original\_data)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🔄 Method 2: inplace=True (Modifies Original)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔧 Method 2: inplace=True (Modifies Original)"}\NormalTok{)  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Store original ID for comparison}
\NormalTok{original\_id }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{id}\NormalTok{(original\_data)}

\CommentTok{\# Add bonus column in place}
\NormalTok{original\_data[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Bonus\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ original\_data[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Salary\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*} \FloatTok{0.1}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"✅ Original DataFrame after in{-}place modification:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(original\_data[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Name\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Salary\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Bonus\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].head(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{))}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"📍 Same DataFrame ID: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{id}\NormalTok{(original\_data)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"🔍 ID unchanged: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{original\_id }\OperatorTok{==} \BuiltInTok{id}\NormalTok{(original\_data)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Common Methods Supporting \texttt{inplace}
Parameter}{Common Methods Supporting inplace Parameter}}\label{common-methods-supporting-inplace-parameter}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📋 Demonstrate inplace with different pandas methods}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🛠️ METHODS SUPPORTING INPLACE PARAMETER"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Create sample dataset for demonstrations}
\NormalTok{sample\_df }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(\{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Laptop\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Phone\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Tablet\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Phone\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Laptop\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{1200}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{800}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{600}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{850}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1100}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Category\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Electronics\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Electronics\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Electronics\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Electronics\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Electronics\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Stock\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{15}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{\})}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 Sample Dataset:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(sample\_df)}

\CommentTok{\# 🗑️ 1. DROP operations}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🗑️ 1. DROP OPERATIONS"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Drop with inplace=False (default)}
\NormalTok{df\_copy }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sample\_df.copy()}
\NormalTok{result }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_copy.drop(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Category\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# inplace=False by default}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"✅ After drop(inplace=False) {-} returns new DataFrame:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_copy}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, New shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Drop with inplace=True  }
\NormalTok{df\_copy2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sample\_df.copy()}
\NormalTok{return\_value }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_copy2.drop(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Category\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, inplace}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{True}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"✅ After drop(inplace=True) {-} modifies original:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Modified shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_copy2}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Return value: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{return\_value}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🏷️ 2. RENAME operations}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🏷️ 2. RENAME OPERATIONS"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{df\_copy3 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sample\_df.copy()}
\CommentTok{\# Rename with inplace=False}
\NormalTok{renamed }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_copy3.rename(columns}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{\{}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Item\_Name\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{\})}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"✅ rename(inplace=False): Original columns unchanged"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(df\_copy3.columns)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"New: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(renamed.columns)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Rename with inplace=True}
\NormalTok{df\_copy3.rename(columns}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{\{}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Item\_Name\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{\}, inplace}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{True}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"✅ rename(inplace=True): Original columns changed"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Modified: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(df\_copy3.columns)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 🔄 3. SORT operations}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔄 3. SORT OPERATIONS"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{df\_copy4 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sample\_df.copy()}
\CommentTok{\# Sort with inplace=False}
\NormalTok{sorted\_df }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_copy4.sort\_values(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"✅ sort\_values(inplace=False):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original order preserved: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(df\_copy4[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"New sorted order: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(sorted\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Sort with inplace=True}
\NormalTok{df\_copy4.sort\_values(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, inplace}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{True}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"✅ sort\_values(inplace=True):"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{survey\_data\_insta[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}num\_insta\_followers\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{survey\_data\_insta[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}num\_insta\_followers\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].}\BuiltInTok{str}\NormalTok{.replace(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}\textasciitilde{}\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}

\end{Shaded}

\chapter{Pandas Intermediate}\label{pandas-intermediate}

Now that you've learned the \textbf{fundamentals of pandas}, this
chapter shifts focus to \textbf{transformations} --- techniques that
reshape and enrich your data.\\
You'll practice vectorized arithmetic, automatic alignment, conditional
logic, and row- vs.~column-wise operations that turn raw tables into
analysis-ready features.

\section{Learning Objective}\label{learning-objective}

At the end of this chapter, you will learn:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Arithmetic Operations} --- perform calculations within and
  between DataFrames\\
\item
  \textbf{Broadcasting} --- apply operations efficiently across
  different shapes with automatic alignment\\
\item
  \textbf{Transformations} --- use \texttt{map()} and \texttt{apply()}
  to transform your data flexibly\\
\item
  \textbf{Lambda Functions} --- create quick, inline transformations
  with \texttt{map()} or \texttt{apply()}\\
\item
  \textbf{Advanced NLP Preprocessing} --- practice transformations that
  support your final project
\end{itemize}

🔑 \textbf{Note on Vectorization:}\\
Vectorization means executing operations in \textbf{parallel} (built on
top of NumPy) instead of using slow Python loops.\\
In this chapter, we will \textbf{motivate NumPy vectorization} and
introduce its benefits. A deeper dive will come in the dedicated
\textbf{NumPy chapter}.

First of all, let's import

\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ numpy }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ np}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ pandas }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ pd}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ time}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\section{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Arithmetic Operations:} Within and
Between
DataFrames}{Arithmetic Operations: Within and Between DataFrames}}\label{arithmetic-operations-within-and-between-dataframes}

Arithmetic operations are essential when working with \textbf{numerical
data columns} in pandas.

\subsection{Why Arithmetic Operations Matter in Data
Science}\label{why-arithmetic-operations-matter-in-data-science}

They form the backbone of many common tasks, including:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Creating new metrics} --- e.g.,
  \texttt{profit\ =\ revenue\ -\ cost}\\
\item
  \textbf{Normalizing data} --- z-scores, percentages, or scaling\\
\item
  \textbf{Comparing datasets} --- growth rates, ratios, or relative
  differences\\
\item
  \textbf{Financial analysis} --- ROI, margins, compound growth\\
\item
  \textbf{Scientific computations} --- applying formulas and
  transformations
\end{itemize}

\textbf{🚀 Pandas Advantage:} Arithmetic in pandas is \textbf{intuitive
and concise} --- operations align automatically by rows and columns,
saving you from manual looping.

\subsection{Arithmetic Operations Within a
DataFrame}\label{arithmetic-operations-within-a-dataframe}

\textbf{Core Concept}: Perform calculations \textbf{between columns},
\textbf{with constants}, or \textbf{across rows}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2340}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.1702}}

Operation
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Symbol

Example
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Business Use Case
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Addition} & \texttt{+} &
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}{]}\ +\ df{[}\textquotesingle{}B\textquotesingle{}{]}}
& Total sales = Online + Retail \\
\textbf{Subtraction} & \texttt{-} &
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}Revenue\textquotesingle{}{]}\ -\ df{[}\textquotesingle{}Cost\textquotesingle{}{]}}
& Profit calculation \\
\textbf{Multiplication} & \texttt{*} &
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}Price\textquotesingle{}{]}\ *\ df{[}\textquotesingle{}Quantity\textquotesingle{}{]}}
& Total value \\
\textbf{Division} & \texttt{/} &
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}Profit\textquotesingle{}{]}\ /\ df{[}\textquotesingle{}Revenue\textquotesingle{}{]}}
& Margin percentage \\
\textbf{Power} & \texttt{**} &
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}Principal\textquotesingle{}{]}\ *\ (1\ +\ rate)**years}
& Compound interest \\
\textbf{Floor Division} & \texttt{//} &
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}Total\textquotesingle{}{]}\ //\ df{[}\textquotesingle{}BatchSize\textquotesingle{}{]}}
& Number of full batches \\
\textbf{Modulo} & \texttt{\%} &
\texttt{df{[}\textquotesingle{}ID\textquotesingle{}{]}\ \%\ 10} &
Grouping by last digit \\

\subsubsection{Column-to-Column
Operations}\label{column-to-column-operations}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Create a business{-}like DataFrame for demonstrations}
\NormalTok{business\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Laptop\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Phone\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Tablet\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Watch\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Headphones\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Units\_Sold\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{150}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{300}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{200}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{500}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{250}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\_per\_Unit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{1200}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{800}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{600}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{400}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{200}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Cost\_per\_Unit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{800}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{500}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{400}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{250}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{120}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Marketing\_Spend\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{15000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{25000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{18000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12000}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{\}}
\NormalTok{business\_df }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(business\_data)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 Original Business Data:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(business\_df)}

\CommentTok{\# 💰 Basic arithmetic operations between columns}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Revenue\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Units\_Sold\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\_per\_Unit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Cost\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Units\_Sold\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Cost\_per\_Unit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]  }
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Revenue\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Cost\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Net\_Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Marketing\_Spend\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}

\CommentTok{\# 📈 Calculate ratios and percentages}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Profit\_Margin\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Revenue\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]) }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{100}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ROI\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Net\_Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Marketing\_Spend\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]) }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{100}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{💡 Enhanced Business Data with Calculations:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(business\_df[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Revenue\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Gross\_Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Net\_Profit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Profit\_Margin\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ROI\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{))}

\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsubsection{Operations with Constants and
Scalars}\label{operations-with-constants-and-scalars}

In pandas, you can perform arithmetic operations not only between
columns, but also with \textbf{constants (scalars)}.\\
The operation is applied \textbf{element-wise} across the entire column
or DataFrame --- thanks to vectorization.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🎯 Operations with constants (scalars)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Operations with Constants:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Apply 10\% discount to all prices}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Discounted\_Price\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\_per\_Unit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*} \FloatTok{0.9}

\CommentTok{\# Add fixed shipping cost of $50 to all products}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\_with\_Shipping\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\_per\_Unit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{50}

\CommentTok{\# Calculate tax (8\% of revenue)}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Tax\_Amount\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Revenue\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*} \FloatTok{0.08}

\CommentTok{\# Square the units sold (for some statistical analysis)}
\NormalTok{business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Units\_Squared\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ business\_df[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Units\_Sold\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{**} \DecValTok{2}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Sample with scalar operations:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{sample\_cols }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\_per\_Unit\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Discounted\_Price\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Price\_with\_Shipping\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Tax\_Amount\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(business\_df[sample\_cols].head(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{).to\_string(index}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Operations with Constants:
Sample with scalar operations:
Product  Price_per_Unit  Discounted_Price  Price_with_Shipping  Tax_Amount
 Laptop            1200            1080.0                 1250     14400.0
  Phone             800             720.0                  850     19200.0
 Tablet             600             540.0                  650      9600.0
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Row-wise Operations (Across
Columns)}\label{row-wise-operations-across-columns}

By default, methods like \texttt{.mean()}, \texttt{.max()}, and
\texttt{.min()} operate \textbf{down each column} (\texttt{axis=0}).\\
However, if you need to perform calculations \textbf{across all columns
in each row}, set \texttt{axis=1}.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📊 Row{-}wise arithmetic operations (axis=1 for across columns)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔄 Row{-}wise Operations:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Create a sample DataFrame with numerical data}
\NormalTok{sample\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q1\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{150}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{200}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{120}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{180}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q2\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{110}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{140}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{220}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{130}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{190}\NormalTok{], }
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q3\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{120}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{160}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{210}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{140}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{200}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q4\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{130}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{170}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{230}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{150}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{210}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{\}}
\NormalTok{quarterly\_sales }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(sample\_data, }
\NormalTok{                              index}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\_A\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\_B\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\_C\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\_D\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Product\_E\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📈 Quarterly Sales Data:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(quarterly\_sales)}

\CommentTok{\# Calculate row{-}wise statistics}
\NormalTok{quarterly\_sales[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Total\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ quarterly\_sales.}\BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# Sum across columns}
\NormalTok{quarterly\_sales[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Average\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ quarterly\_sales[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q1\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q2\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q3\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q4\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].mean(axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{quarterly\_sales[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Max\_Quarter\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ quarterly\_sales[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q1\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q2\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q3\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q4\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{(axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{quarterly\_sales[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Sales\_Range\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ quarterly\_sales[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q1\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q2\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q3\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q4\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{(axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ quarterly\_sales[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q1\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q2\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q3\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q4\_Sales\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].}\BuiltInTok{min}\NormalTok{(axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📊 With Row{-}wise Calculations:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(quarterly\_sales.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Arithmetic Operations Between
DataFrames}\label{arithmetic-operations-between-dataframes}

\textbf{Key Concept}: When operating on \textbf{two DataFrames}, pandas
\textbf{automatically aligns} data by \textbf{index} and \textbf{column
labels}.

\subsubsection{Alignment Behavior}\label{alignment-behavior}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3571}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3214}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3214}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Scenario
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Result
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Example
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Exact match} & Normal operation & \texttt{df1\ +\ df2} \\
\textbf{Missing index/column} & Fills with \texttt{NaN} & Automatic
alignment \\
\textbf{Different shapes} & Broadcasts when possible & Scalar
operations \\
\textbf{Using fill\_value} & Replaces NaN with specified value &
\texttt{df1.add(df2,\ fill\_value=0)} \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{💡 Pro Tip}: Use \textbf{explicit methods} (\texttt{add()},
\texttt{sub()}, \texttt{mul()}, \texttt{div()}) for better control over
missing data!

\subsubsection{Basic DataFrame-to-DataFrame
Operations}\label{basic-dataframe-to-dataframe-operations}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🏢 Create two related business DataFrames for comparison}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔀 DataFrame{-}to{-}DataFrame Operations:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 📊 Store A performance data}
\NormalTok{store\_a\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Electronics\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{50000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{55000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{60000}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Clothing\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{30000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{32000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{35000}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Books\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{8000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8500}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{9000}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{\}}
\NormalTok{store\_a }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(store\_a\_data, index}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q2\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q3\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}

\CommentTok{\# 📊 Store B performance data  }
\NormalTok{store\_b\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Electronics\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{45000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{58000}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Clothing\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{28000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{33000}\NormalTok{],}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Books\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: [}\DecValTok{7500}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8800}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{\}}
\NormalTok{store\_b }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(store\_b\_data, index}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q1\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q2\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Q3\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🏪 Store A Sales:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(store\_a)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{🏪 Store B Sales:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(store\_b)}

\CommentTok{\# 📈 Basic arithmetic operations between DataFrames}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{💡 Arithmetic Operations Between Stores:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Total sales across both stores}
\NormalTok{total\_sales }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ store\_a }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ store\_b}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📊 Combined Sales (A + B):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(total\_sales)}

\CommentTok{\# Difference in performance}
\NormalTok{sales\_diff }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ store\_a }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ store\_b  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📊 Sales Difference (A {-} B):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(sales\_diff)}

\CommentTok{\# Growth ratio (Store A relative to Store B)}
\NormalTok{growth\_ratio }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ store\_a }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ store\_b}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{📊 Performance Ratio (A / B):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(growth\_ratio.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

🏪 Store A Sales:
    Electronics  Clothing  Books
Q1        50000     30000   8000
Q2        55000     32000   8500
Q3        60000     35000   9000

🏪 Store B Sales:
    Electronics  Clothing  Books
Q1        45000     28000   7500
