\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Sentiment Analysis: Understanding
Emotions}}{Sentiment Analysis: Understanding Emotions}}\label{sentiment-analysis-understanding-emotions}

NLTK provides powerful tools for analyzing sentiment - determining
whether text expresses positive, negative, or neutral emotions.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 📊 Sentiment Analysis with NLTK VADER}
\ImportTok{from}\NormalTok{ nltk.sentiment }\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ SentimentIntensityAnalyzer}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ pandas }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ pd}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ matplotlib.pyplot }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ plt}
\NormalTok{nltk.download(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}vader\_lexicon\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Initialize VADER sentiment analyzer}
\NormalTok{analyzer }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()}

\CommentTok{\# Diverse sample texts for sentiment analysis}
\NormalTok{sample\_texts }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}
    \CommentTok{\# Positive examples}
    \StringTok{"This product is absolutely amazing! I love everything about it!"}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{"Fantastic customer service and fast delivery. Highly recommend!"}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{"Great value for money. Very satisfied with my purchase."}\NormalTok{,}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Negative examples  }
    \StringTok{"Terrible quality, waste of money. Very disappointed."}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{"Poor customer service and the product broke immediately."}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{"Worst purchase I\textquotesingle{}ve ever made. Completely useless."}\NormalTok{,}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Neutral examples}
    \StringTok{"The product arrived on time. It\textquotesingle{}s okay, nothing special."}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{"Standard quality for the price. Does what it\textquotesingle{}s supposed to do."}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{"Average product with typical features. Works as expected."}\NormalTok{,}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Mixed sentiment}
    \StringTok{"Great design but poor durability. Mixed feelings about this."}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{"Love the features but hate the price. It\textquotesingle{}s complicated."}\NormalTok{,}
\NormalTok{]}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 SENTIMENT ANALYSIS WITH NLTK VADER"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Analyze sentiment for each text}
\NormalTok{sentiment\_results }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i, text }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{enumerate}\NormalTok{(sample\_texts, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{):}
    \CommentTok{\# Get sentiment scores}
\NormalTok{    scores }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ analyzer.polarity\_scores(text)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Determine overall sentiment}
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \FloatTok{0.05}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{        overall }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Positive\textquotesingle{}}
\NormalTok{        emoji }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}😊\textquotesingle{}}
    \ControlFlowTok{elif}\NormalTok{ scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{\textless{}=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\FloatTok{0.05}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{        overall }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Negative\textquotesingle{}}  
\NormalTok{        emoji }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}😞\textquotesingle{}}
    \ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{        overall }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Neutral\textquotesingle{}}
\NormalTok{        emoji }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}😐\textquotesingle{}}
    
\NormalTok{    sentiment\_results.append(\{}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Text\_ID\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\SpecialStringTok{f\textquotesingle{}Text\_}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{i}\SpecialCharTok{:02d\}}\SpecialStringTok{\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Text\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: text[:}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{"..."} \ControlFlowTok{if} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(text) }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{50} \ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{ text,}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Positive\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}pos\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{),}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Neutral\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}neu\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{), }
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Negative\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}neg\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{),}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{], }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{),}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Sentiment\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: overall,}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Emoji\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: emoji,}
        \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Full\_Text\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: text}
\NormalTok{    \})}
    
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{emoji}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ Text }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{i}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{overall}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (compound: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   }\CharTok{\textbackslash{}"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{text}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}"}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   Pos: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}pos\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Neu: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}neu\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Neg: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}neg\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# Create DataFrame for analysis}
\NormalTok{df\_sentiment }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(sentiment\_results)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📈 SENTIMENT ANALYSIS SUMMARY"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Overall statistics}
\NormalTok{sentiment\_counts }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Sentiment\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].value\_counts()}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 Sentiment Distribution:"}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ sentiment, count }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ sentiment\_counts.items():}
\NormalTok{    percentage }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (count }\OperatorTok{/} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(df\_sentiment)) }\OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{100}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"  }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{sentiment}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{count}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ texts (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{percentage}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{\%)"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📏 Score Ranges:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"• Positive scores: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Positive\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{min}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Positive\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"• Negative scores: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Negative\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{min}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Negative\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"• Compound scores: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{min}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ {-} }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{()}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Show most extreme examples}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🎯 Most Extreme Examples:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{most\_positive }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_sentiment.loc[df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].idxmax()]}
\NormalTok{most\_negative }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_sentiment.loc[df\_sentiment[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{].idxmin()]}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"😊 Most Positive (score: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{most\_positive[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   }\CharTok{\textbackslash{}"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{most\_positive[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Full\_Text\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}"}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"😞 Most Negative (score: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{most\_negative[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{:.3f\}}\SpecialStringTok{):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   }\CharTok{\textbackslash{}"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{most\_negative[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Full\_Text\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}"}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Business application example}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{💼 Business Application Example:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"This could be used for:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Customer review analysis"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Social media monitoring"}\NormalTok{) }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Product feedback categorization"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Brand sentiment tracking"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Customer support prioritization"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Display summary table}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📋 Detailed Results:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{display\_df }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ df\_sentiment[[}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Text\_ID\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Text\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Compound\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Sentiment\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Emoji\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]].copy()}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(display\_df.to\_string(index}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{Part-of-Speech (POS) Tagging \&
Named Entity
Recognition}}{Part-of-Speech (POS) Tagging \& Named Entity Recognition}}\label{part-of-speech-pos-tagging-named-entity-recognition}

POS tagging identifies grammatical roles of words (noun, verb,
adjective), while Named Entity Recognition (NER) finds important
entities like names, places, and organizations.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🏷️ POS Tagging and Named Entity Recognition}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ nltk}
\ImportTok{from}\NormalTok{ nltk.tokenize }\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ word\_tokenize}
\ImportTok{from}\NormalTok{ nltk.tag }\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ pos\_tag}
\ImportTok{from}\NormalTok{ nltk.chunk }\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ ne\_chunk}
\ImportTok{from}\NormalTok{ nltk.tree }\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ Tree}
\NormalTok{nltk.download(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}averaged\_perceptron\_tagger\_eng\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{nltk.download(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}maxent\_ne\_chunker\_tab\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{nltk.download(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}maxent\_ne\_chunker\_tab\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{nltk.download(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}words\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{nltk.download(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}words\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}


\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ pandas }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ pd}

\CommentTok{\# Sample business{-}related text}
\NormalTok{business\_text }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{"""}
\StringTok{Apple Inc. is planning to open a new headquarters in Austin, Texas next year.}
\StringTok{CEO Tim Cook announced this during a meeting with investors on Wall Street.}
\StringTok{The company expects to hire 5,000 new employees, including software engineers }
\StringTok{and data scientists. Microsoft and Google are also expanding their operations}
\StringTok{in the region. The project will cost approximately $1 billion dollars.}
\StringTok{"""}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🏷️ POS TAGGING \& NAMED ENTITY RECOGNITION"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📝 Sample Text:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(business\_text.strip())}

\CommentTok{\# 1. POS TAGGING}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔤 PART{-}OF{-}SPEECH TAGGING:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{tokens }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ word\_tokenize(business\_text)}
\NormalTok{pos\_tags }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pos\_tag(tokens)}

\CommentTok{\# Group by POS types for analysis}
\NormalTok{pos\_groups }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{\}}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ word, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_tags:}
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ pos }\KeywordTok{not} \KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_groups:}
\NormalTok{        pos\_groups[pos] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
\NormalTok{    pos\_groups[pos].append(word)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Found }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{set}\NormalTok{([pos }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ \_, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_tags]))}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ different POS tags:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Show most common POS categories}
\NormalTok{pos\_description }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}NN\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Noun (singular)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}NNS\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Noun (plural)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}NNP\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Proper noun (singular)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}NNPS\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Proper noun (plural)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}VB\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Verb (base form)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}VBD\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Verb (past tense)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}VBG\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Verb (gerund/present participle)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}VBN\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Verb (past participle)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}VBP\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Verb (present, not 3rd person singular)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}VBZ\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Verb (present, 3rd person singular)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}JJ\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Adjective\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}JJR\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Adjective (comparative)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}JJS\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Adjective (superlative)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}RB\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Adverb\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}DT\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Determiner\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}IN\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Preposition/subordinating conjunction\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}TO\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}to\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}CD\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Cardinal number\textquotesingle{}}
\NormalTok{\}}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ pos }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{sorted}\NormalTok{(pos\_groups.keys()):}
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_description:}
\NormalTok{        example\_words }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pos\_groups[pos][:}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]  }\CommentTok{\# Show first 3 examples}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"  }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{pos}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{pos\_description[pos]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{example\_words}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 2. NAMED ENTITY RECOGNITION  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🏢 NAMED ENTITY RECOGNITION:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{named\_entities }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ne\_chunk(pos\_tags)}

\CommentTok{\# Extract entities}
\NormalTok{entities }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
\KeywordTok{def}\NormalTok{ extract\_entities(tree):}
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ subtree }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ tree:}
        \ControlFlowTok{if} \BuiltInTok{isinstance}\NormalTok{(subtree, Tree):  }\CommentTok{\# It\textquotesingle{}s a named entity}
\NormalTok{            entity\_name }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{} \textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{.join([token }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ token, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ subtree.leaves()])}
\NormalTok{            entity\_label }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ subtree.label()}
\NormalTok{            entities.append((entity\_name, entity\_label))}
            
\NormalTok{extract\_entities(named\_entities)}

\ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ entities:}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🎯 Detected Entities:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{    entity\_types }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{\}}
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ entity, label }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ entities:}
        \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ label }\KeywordTok{not} \KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ entity\_types:}
\NormalTok{            entity\_types[label] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
\NormalTok{        entity\_types[label].append(entity)}
    
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ label, entity\_list }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ entity\_types.items():}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"  }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{label}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{entity\_list}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{:}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"  No named entities detected with basic NER"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 3. MANUAL ENTITY EXTRACTION (for demonstration)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔍 MANUAL ENTITY IDENTIFICATION:"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Find potential entities using POS tags}
\NormalTok{companies }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [word }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ word, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_tags }\ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ pos }\OperatorTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}NNP\textquotesingle{}} \KeywordTok{and}\NormalTok{ word }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Apple\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Microsoft\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Google\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\NormalTok{people }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [word }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ word, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_tags }\ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ pos }\OperatorTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}NNP\textquotesingle{}} \KeywordTok{and}\NormalTok{ word }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Tim\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Cook\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\NormalTok{locations }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [word }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ word, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_tags }\ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ pos }\OperatorTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}NNP\textquotesingle{}} \KeywordTok{and}\NormalTok{ word }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Austin\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Texas\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Wall\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Street\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]]}
\NormalTok{numbers }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [word }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ word, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_tags }\ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ pos }\OperatorTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}CD\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}

\NormalTok{manual\_entities }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Companies\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: companies,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}People\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: people,}
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Locations\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: locations, }
    \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Numbers\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: numbers}
\NormalTok{\}}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ category, items }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ manual\_entities.items():}
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ items:}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"  }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{category}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{items}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 4. BUSINESS APPLICATIONS}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{💼 BUSINESS APPLICATIONS:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"POS Tagging can be used for:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Information extraction from documents"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Improving search relevance"}\NormalTok{)  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Text summarization"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Grammar checking tools"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Keyword extraction"}\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{Named Entity Recognition can be used for:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Customer relationship management"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Compliance and regulatory analysis"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• News and social media monitoring"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Document classification"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Knowledge graph construction"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Create summary DataFrame}
\NormalTok{word\_analysis }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ word, pos }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ pos\_tags[:}\DecValTok{15}\NormalTok{]:  }\CommentTok{\# First 15 words}
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ word.isalpha():  }\CommentTok{\# Skip punctuation}
\NormalTok{        is\_entity }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{any}\NormalTok{(word }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ entity }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ entity, \_ }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ entities)}
\NormalTok{        word\_analysis.append(\{}
            \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Word\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: word,}
            \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}POS\_Tag\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: pos,}
            \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}POS\_Description\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: pos\_description.get(pos, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Other\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{),}
            \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Is\_Entity\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{: is\_entity}
\NormalTok{        \})}

\NormalTok{df\_analysis }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ pd.DataFrame(word\_analysis)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{📋 Sample Word Analysis:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(df\_analysis.to\_string(index}\OperatorTok{=}\VariableTok{False}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{\textbf{💡 Best Practices \&
Tips}}{💡 Best Practices \& Tips}}\label{best-practices-tips}

\textbf{Performance Optimization:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Use \textbf{stemming} for speed-critical applications\\
\item
  Use \textbf{lemmatization} for accuracy-critical applications
\item
  \textbf{Cache} processed results for repeated text analysis
\item
  \textbf{Batch process} large datasets instead of one-by-one
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Data Quality:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Clean text} before processing (remove HTML, special
  characters)
\item
  \textbf{Handle multiple languages} appropriately
\item
  \textbf{Validate results} with domain experts
\item
  \textbf{Consider context} when interpreting sentiment
\end{itemize}

NLTK provides an excellent foundation for understanding NLP concepts
before moving to more advanced tools!

\subsection{Practice exercise 1}\label{practice-exercise-1-1}

\subsubsection{}\label{section-23}

Read the file \emph{STAT303-1 survey for data analysis.csv}.

\subsubsection{}\label{section-24}

Rename all the columns of the data, except the first two columns, with
the shorter names in the list \texttt{new\_col\_names} given below. The
order of column names in the list is the same as the order in which the
columns are to be renamed starting with the third column from the left.

\begin{Highlighting}[]

}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}do\_you\_smoke\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}weed\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}are\_you\_an\_introvert\_or\_extrovert\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}love\_first\_sight\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}learning\_style\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}left\_right\_brained\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}personality\_type\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}social\_media\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}num\_insta\_followers\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}streaming\_platforms\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}expected\_marriage\_age\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}expected\_starting\_salary\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, \chapter{NumPy Fundamentals}\label{numpy-fundamentals}

\pandocbounded{\includegraphics[keepaspectratio]{index_files/mediabag/mg8O3kd.png}}

\textbf{NumPy} is a foundational library in Python, providing support
for large, multi-dimensional arrays and matrices, along with a variety
of mathematical functions. It's a critical tool in data science and
machine learning because it enables efficient numerical computations,
data manipulation, and linear algebra operations. Many data science
packcages and machine learning algorithms rely on these operations to
process data and perform complex calculations quickly. Moreover, popular
libraries like \texttt{Pandas}, \texttt{SciPy}, and \texttt{TensorFlow}
are built on top of NumPy, making it essential to understand for
implementing and optimizing machine learning models.

\section{Learning Objectives}\label{learning-objectives-3}

By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to:

\subsection{Foundation Skills}\label{foundation-skills}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Create NumPy arrays} using various methods
  (\texttt{np.array()}, \texttt{np.zeros()}, \texttt{np.arange()}, etc.)
\item
  \textbf{Understand array attributes} (\texttt{shape}, \texttt{dtype},
  \texttt{size}, \texttt{ndim}) and their importance
\item
  \textbf{Master indexing and slicing} for extracting and modifying
  array elements
\item
  \textbf{Implement efficient array reshaping} and concatenation
  techniques\\
\item
  \textbf{Choose appropriate data types} to minimize memory usage
\end{itemize}

\section{Getting Started with NumPy}\label{getting-started-with-numpy}

\section{Why NumPy?}\label{why-numpy}

Think of NumPy arrays as an upgrade to Python's built-in lists and
tuples.\\
You can store data in them and perform the same kinds of
computations---but with a big advantage:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Memory Savings}: Arrays use a fixed, compact layout in memory,
  reducing overhead.
\item
  \textbf{Efficiency}: NumPy is optimized at the C level, making it far
  faster than pure Python structures.\\
\item
  \textbf{Scalability}: Designed to handle large datasets smoothly
  without slowing down.
\end{itemize}

👉 This is why NumPy is the backbone of scientific computing and data
science in Python.

\subsection{NumPy Arrays are Memory Efficient: Homogeneity \& Contiguous
Storage}\label{numpy-arrays-are-memory-efficient-homogeneity-contiguous-storage}

A \textbf{NumPy array} stores elements of the \textbf{same data type} in
\textbf{contiguous memory locations}.\\
This contrasts with Python lists, which can hold mixed data types and
store elements in scattered memory locations.

Because of this:\\
- NumPy arrays are \textbf{densely packed}, minimizing memory
overhead.\\
- Operations can be executed much faster, since data is laid out
predictably in memory.

👉 The result: \textbf{lower memory consumption} and \textbf{higher
performance} when working with large datasets.

The following example compares the memory usage of NumPy arrays with
Python lists.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ sys}

\CommentTok{\# Create a NumPy array, Python list, and tuple with the same elements}
\NormalTok{array }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.arange(}\DecValTok{1000}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{py\_list }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1000}\NormalTok{))}
\NormalTok{py\_tuple }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{tuple}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1000}\NormalTok{))}

\CommentTok{\# Calculate memory usage}
\NormalTok{array\_memory }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ array.nbytes}
\NormalTok{list\_memory }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sys.getsizeof(py\_list) }\OperatorTok{+} \BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(sys.getsizeof(item) }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ item }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ py\_list)}
\NormalTok{tuple\_memory }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ sys.getsizeof(py\_tuple) }\OperatorTok{+} \BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(sys.getsizeof(item) }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ item }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ py\_tuple)}

\CommentTok{\# Display the memory usage}
\NormalTok{memory\_usage }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \StringTok{"NumPy Array (in bytes)"}\NormalTok{: array\_memory,}
    \StringTok{"Python List (in bytes)"}\NormalTok{: list\_memory,}
    \StringTok{"Python Tuple (in bytes)"}\NormalTok{: tuple\_memory}
\NormalTok{\}}

\NormalTok{memory\_usage}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
{'NumPy Array (in bytes)': 8000,
 'Python List (in bytes)': 36056,
 'Python Tuple (in bytes)': 36040}
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# each element in the array is a 64{-}bit integer}
\NormalTok{array.dtype}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
dtype('int64')
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{NumPy arrays are fast}\label{numpy-arrays-are-fast}

NumPy arrays enable mathematical computations to run much faster than
with native Python data structures. This speed advantage comes from
three key factors:

\begin{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Densely Packed \& Homogeneous Data}\\
  Since NumPy arrays store elements of the same type in contiguous
  memory, data retrieval is faster and computations can be executed more
  efficiently.
\item
  \textbf{Vectorized Computations}\\
  NumPy replaces slow Python \texttt{for} loops with \textbf{vectorized
  operations}, which are internally broken into optimized fragments and
  executed in parallel. This means calculations are applied to entire
  arrays at once, rather than element by element.
\item
  \textbf{Integration with C/C++}\\
  Under the hood, NumPy is implemented in \textbf{C and C++}, which are
  compiled languages with very low execution overhead compared to
  Python. This gives NumPy both the speed of C and the usability of
  Python.
\end{itemize}

We'll see the faster speed on NumPy computations in the example below.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\KeywordTok{def}\NormalTok{ my\_dot(a, b): }
    \CommentTok{"""}
\CommentTok{   Compute the dot product of two vectors}
\CommentTok{ }
\CommentTok{    Args:}
\CommentTok{      a (ndarray (n,)):  input vector }
\CommentTok{      b (ndarray (n,)):  input vector with same dimension as a}
\CommentTok{    }
\CommentTok{    Returns:}
\CommentTok{      x (scalar): }
\CommentTok{    """}
\NormalTok{    x}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(a.shape[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]):}
\NormalTok{        x }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ x }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ a[i] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ b[i]}
    \ControlFlowTok{return}\NormalTok{ x}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{np.random.seed(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{a }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.rand(}\DecValTok{10000000}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# very large arrays}
\NormalTok{b }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.rand(}\DecValTok{10000000}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{tic }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()  }\CommentTok{\# capture start time}
\NormalTok{c }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.dot(a, b)}
\NormalTok{toc }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()  }\CommentTok{\# capture end time}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"np.dot(a, b) =  }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{c}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Vectorized version duration: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\DecValTok{1000}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{(toc}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{tic)}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ ms "}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{tic }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()  }\CommentTok{\# capture start time}
\NormalTok{c }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ my\_dot(a,b)}
\NormalTok{toc }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()  }\CommentTok{\# capture end time}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"my\_dot(a, b) =  }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{c}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"loop version duration: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\DecValTok{1000}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{(toc}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{tic)}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ ms "}\NormalTok{)}

\KeywordTok{del}\NormalTok{(a)}\OperatorTok{;}\KeywordTok{del}\NormalTok{(b)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
np.dot(a, b) =  2501072.5817
Vectorized version duration: 0.0000 ms 
my_dot(a, b) =  2501072.5817
loop version duration: 1695.4978 ms 
\end{verbatim}

✅ \textbf{Both methods produce the same result, but the vectorized
\texttt{np.dot()} executes almost instantly, while the manual Python
loop takes over a second.}

👉 This clearly demonstrates how NumPy's \textbf{vectorization} and
\textbf{C backend} make computations orders of magnitude faster than
pure Python loops.

\CommentTok{\# Arrays of zeros and ones}
\NormalTok{zeros\_3x3 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.zeros((}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{))}
\NormalTok{ones\_2x4 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.ones((}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{))}
\NormalTok{full\_matrix }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.full((}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{), }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# Fill with custom value}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Zeros (3x3):}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{zeros\_3x3}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Ones (2x4):}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{ones\_2x4}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Full of 7s:}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{full\_matrix}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Identity matrix}
\NormalTok{identity }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.eye(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Identity matrix:}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{identity}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Understanding Array
Attributes}\label{understanding-array-attributes}

Let us define a NumPy array in order to access its attributes:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{numpy\_ex }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{],[}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{,}\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{]])}
\NormalTok{numpy\_ex}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
array([[1, 2, 3],
       [4, 5, 6]])
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\BuiltInTok{type}\NormalTok{(numpy\_ex)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
numpy.ndarray
\end{verbatim}

It is an \textbf{ndarray} type.

You can explore the attributes and methods of \texttt{numpy\_ex} by
typing:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{numpy\_ex.}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

and then pressing the \emph{tab} key.

Some of the basic attributes of a NumPy array are the following:

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\href{https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.ndim.html}{\texttt{ndim}}}{ndim}}\label{ndim}

Shows the number of dimensions (or axes) of the array.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{numpy\_ex.ndim}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
2
\end{verbatim}

Numpy arrays can have any number of dimensions and different lengths
along each dimension. We can inspect the length along each dimension
using the \texttt{.shape} property of an array.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\href{https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.shape.html}{\texttt{shape}}}{shape}}\label{shape}

This is a tuple of integers indicating the size of the array in each
dimension. For a matrix with \emph{n} rows and \emph{m} columns, the
shape will be \emph{(n,m)}. The length of the shape tuple is therefore
the rank, or the number of dimensions, \texttt{ndim}.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{numpy\_ex.shape}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
(2, 3)
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\href{https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.size.html}{\texttt{size}}}{size}}\label{size}

This is the total number of elements of the array, which is the product
of the elements of shape.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{numpy\_ex.size}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
6
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\href{https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.ndarray.dtype.html}{\texttt{dtype}}}{dtype}}\label{dtype}

Unlike lists and tuples, NumPy arrays are designed to store elements of
the same type, enabling more efficient memory usage and faster
computations. The data type of the elements in a NumPy array can be
accessed using the \texttt{.dtype} attribute

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{numpy\_ex.dtype}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
dtype('int64')
\end{verbatim}

\section{Data Types and Memory
Optimization}\label{data-types-and-memory-optimization}

NumPy supports a wide range of data types, each with a defined memory
size. These types map directly to \textbf{C data types}, since NumPy is
implemented in C at its computational core.\\
This design allows NumPy to handle array operations far more efficiently
than native Python data structures.

\subsection{Common NumPy Data Types}\label{common-numpy-data-types}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\textbf{Data Type} & \textbf{Memory Size} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{np.int8} & 1 byte \\
\texttt{np.int16} & 2 bytes \\
\texttt{np.int32} & 4 bytes \\
\texttt{np.int64} & 8 bytes \\
\texttt{np.uint8} & 1 byte \\
\texttt{np.uint16} & 2 bytes \\
\texttt{np.uint32} & 4 bytes \\
\texttt{np.uint64} & 8 bytes \\
\texttt{np.float16} & 2 bytes \\
\texttt{np.float32} & 4 bytes \\
\texttt{np.float64} & 8 bytes \\
\texttt{np.complex64} & 8 bytes \\
\texttt{np.complex128} & 16 bytes \\
\texttt{np.bool\_} & 1 byte \\
\texttt{np.string\_} & 1 byte per character \\
\texttt{np.unicode\_} & 4 bytes per character \\
\texttt{np.object\_} & Variable (Python objects) \\
\texttt{np.datetime64} & 8 bytes \\
\texttt{np.timedelta64} & 8 bytes \\
\end{longtable}

💡 \textbf{Tip:} Choosing the right data type is crucial for
\textbf{memory efficiency} and \textbf{performance}. For large datasets,
using smaller types (e.g., \texttt{int16} instead of \texttt{int64}) can
save significant memory.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Add practical examples for data type selection}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 CHOOSING THE RIGHT DATA TYPE"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Memory efficiency example}
\NormalTok{large\_numbers }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{1000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3000}\NormalTok{], dtype}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{np.int16)  }\CommentTok{\# Efficient for small ranges}
\NormalTok{small\_numbers }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{], dtype}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{np.int8)           }\CommentTok{\# Very memory efficient}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"int16 array memory: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{large\_numbers}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{nbytes}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ bytes"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"int8 array memory: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{small\_numbers}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{nbytes}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ bytes"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Precision example  }
\NormalTok{high\_precision }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\FloatTok{3.14159265359}\NormalTok{], dtype}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{np.float64)}
\NormalTok{low\_precision }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\FloatTok{3.14159265359}\NormalTok{], dtype}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{np.float32)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"float64 precision: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{high\_precision}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"float32 precision: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{low\_precision}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
📊 CHOOSING THE RIGHT DATA TYPE
========================================
int16 array memory: 6 bytes
int8 array memory: 3 bytes
float64 precision: [3.14159265]
float32 precision: [3.1415927]
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Upcasting}\label{upcasting}

When you create a NumPy array with elements of different data types,
NumPy automatically \textbf{upcasts} them to a common type that can
represent all values.\\
This process---also called \textbf{type coercion} or \textbf{type
promotion}---follows a hierarchy of data types to prevent data loss.

Below are two common cases of upcasting, with examples:

\textbf{Numeric Upcasting}: If you mix integers and floats, NumPy will
convert the entire array to floats.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{arr }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{2.5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(arr.dtype)  }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
float64
\end{verbatim}

\textbf{String Upcasting}: If you mix numbers and strings, NumPy will
upcast all elements to strings.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{arr }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}hello\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{3.5}\NormalTok{])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(arr.dtype)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
<U32
\end{verbatim}

\section{Array Indexing and Slicing: Accessing Your
Data}\label{array-indexing-and-slicing-accessing-your-data}

\subsection{Array Indexing}\label{array-indexing}

Similar to Python lists, NumPy uses zero-based indexing, meaning the
first element of an array is accessed using index \texttt{0}. You can
use positive or negative indices to access elements

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{array }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{])  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]) }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{])  }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
10
50
50
30
\end{verbatim}

In multi-dimensional arrays, indices are separated by commas. The first
index refers to the row, and the second index refers to the column in a
2D array.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 2D array (3 rows, 3 columns)}
\NormalTok{array\_2d }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{], [}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{], [}\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{]])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array\_2d)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array\_2d[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array\_2d[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]) }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array\_2d[}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])  }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
[[1 2 3]
 [4 5 6]
 [7 8 9]]
2
6
9
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Array Slicing}\label{array-slicing}

Slicing is used to extract a sub-array from an existing array.

The Syntax for slicing is `array{[}start:stop:step{]}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{array }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{])  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[:}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{])  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{:])  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[::}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{])  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[::}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]) }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
[20 30 40]
[10 20 30]
[30 40 50]
[10 30 50]
[50 40 30 20 10]
\end{verbatim}

For slicing in Multi-Dimensional Arrays, use commas to separate slicing
for different dimensions

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#\#\#  Indexing \& Slicing Quick Reference}

\CommentTok{\# Extract a sub{-}array: elements from the first two rows and the first two columns}
\NormalTok{sub\_array }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ array\_2d[:}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, :}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(sub\_array)  }

\CommentTok{\# Extract all rows for the second column}
\NormalTok{col }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ array\_2d[:, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(col) }

\CommentTok{\# Extract the last two rows and last two columns}
\NormalTok{sub\_array }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ array\_2d[}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{:, }\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{:]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(sub\_array)  }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Highlighting}
\textcolor{black}{NameError: name 'array_2d' is not defined}
\textcolor{black}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor16}{---------------------------------------------------------------------------}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor16}{NameError}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{                                 Traceback (most recent call last)}
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor4}{Cell}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor4}{ }\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{In[88]}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{, line 4}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{      1}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{ }\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor10}{###  Indexing & Slicing Quick Reference}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{      2}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{ }
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{      3}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{ }\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor10}{# Extract a sub-array: elements from the first two rows and the first two columns}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{----> }\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{4}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{ sub_array = }\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{array_2d}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{[:}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{2}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{, :}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{2}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{]}
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{      5}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{ }\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor7}{print}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{(sub_array)  }
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor6}{      7}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{ }\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor10}{# Extract all rows for the second column}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}
\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor16}{NameError}\textcolor{QuartoInternalColor2}{: name 'array_2d' is not defined}
\end{Highlighting}

The \texttt{step} parameter can be used to select elements at regular
intervals.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#\#\#  Conditional Selection with \textasciigrave{}np.where()\textasciigrave{} and \textasciigrave{}np.select()\textasciigrave{}}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{:}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]) }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array[::}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{])  }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
[1 3 5 7]
[9 7 5 3 1]
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Combining Indexing and
Slicing}\label{combining-indexing-and-slicing}

You can combine indexing and slicing to extract specific elements or
sub-arrays

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Create a 3D array}
\NormalTok{array\_3d }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{], [}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{]], [[}\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{], [}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{11}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{]]])}

\CommentTok{\# Select specific elements and slices}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array\_3d[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, :, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])  }\CommentTok{\# Output: [2 5] (second element from each row in the first sub{-}array)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(array\_3d[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, :}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{])  }\CommentTok{\# Output: [10 11] (first two elements in the last row of the second sub{-}array)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
[2 5]
[10 11]
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Boolean Mask: Conditional
Selection}\label{boolean-mask-conditional-selection}

You can use boolean arrays to filter or select elements based on a
condition

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{a }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{mask }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ a }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{25}                \CommentTok{\# [False False  True  True  True]}
\NormalTok{filtered }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ a[mask]           }\CommentTok{\# [30 40 50]}
\CommentTok{\# one{-}liner:}
\NormalTok{a[a }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{25}\NormalTok{]  }\CommentTok{\# Output: [40 50]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
array([30, 40, 50])
\end{verbatim}

Use bitwise operators with parentheses: \texttt{\&} (and),
\texttt{\textbar{}} (or), \texttt{\textasciitilde{}} (not),
\texttt{\^{}} (xor).

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(a[(a }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{15}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (a }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{)] )     }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(a[(a }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{|}\NormalTok{ (a }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)]  )   }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(a[}\OperatorTok{\textasciitilde{}}\NormalTok{(a }\OperatorTok{\%} \DecValTok{20} \OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)] )}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
[20 30 40]
[10 50]
[10 30 50]
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Indexing \& Slicing Quick
Reference}\label{indexing-slicing-quick-reference}

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\textbf{Operation} & \textbf{Syntax} & \textbf{Example} &
\textbf{Result} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Single element & \texttt{arr{[}i{]}} & \texttt{arr{[}2{]}} & Element at
index 2 \\
Negative indexing & \texttt{arr{[}-i{]}} & \texttt{arr{[}-1{]}} & Last
element \\
Basic slice & \texttt{arr{[}start:stop{]}} & \texttt{arr{[}1:4{]}} &
Elements 1, 2, 3 \\
Step slice & \texttt{arr{[}start:stop:step{]}} & \texttt{arr{[}::2{]}} &
Every 2nd element \\
2D indexing & \texttt{arr{[}row,\ col{]}} & \texttt{arr{[}0,\ 1{]}} &
Row 0, Column 1 \\
Boolean mask & \texttt{arr{[}condition{]}} &
\texttt{arr{[}arr\ \textgreater{}\ 5{]}} & Elements \textgreater{} 5 \\
\end{longtable}

\section{Advanced Selection Methods}\label{advanced-selection-methods}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Conditional Selection with
\texttt{np.where()} and
\texttt{np.select()}}{Conditional Selection with np.where() and np.select()}}\label{conditional-selection-with-np.where-and-np.select}

Use these NumPy tools for fast, vectorized \textbf{if/else} logic on
arrays---perfect for data cleaning, feature engineering, and conditional
transforms.

\textbf{What you can do} - \textbf{Replace values} based on a
condition\\
- \textbf{Choose between arrays} element-wise\\
- \textbf{Apply multi-way logic} (if/elif/else) without loops

\textbf{When to use which} - \texttt{np.where(condition,\ x,\ y)}:
simple \textbf{two-way} branching (or \texttt{np.where(condition)} to
get indices). -
\texttt{np.select({[}cond1,\ cond2,\ ...{]},\ {[}choice1,\ choice2,\ ...{]},\ default=...)}:
clean \textbf{multi-branch} logic (3+ cases).

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{np.where()}}{np.where()}}\label{np.where}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Two forms}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    \texttt{np.where(condition)} → returns the \textbf{indices} where
    \texttt{condition} is \texttt{True}.
  \item
    \texttt{np.where(condition,\ x,\ y)} → \textbf{element-wise choose}:
    pick from \texttt{x} where \texttt{condition} is \texttt{True}, else
    from \texttt{y}.
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Chainable}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    You can \textbf{nest} multiple \texttt{np.where()} calls, but prefer
    \texttt{np.select} for \textbf{3+ branches}.
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Let\textquotesingle{}s create sample data for our examples}
\NormalTok{ages }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{22}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{25}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{19}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{35}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{28}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{24}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{31}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{26}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{23}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{29}\NormalTok{])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Student ages: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{ages}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{scores }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{95}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{87}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{76}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{63}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{89}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{92}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{78}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{85}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{91}\NormalTok{])}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Student scores: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Student ages: [22 25 19 35 28 24 31 26 23 29]
Student scores: [95 87 76 63 89 92 45 78 85 91]
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 USING np.where()"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 1) Simple conditional replacement: scores \textless{} 70 {-}\textgreater{} 0}
\NormalTok{pass\_fail }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.where(scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{70}\NormalTok{, scores, }\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{1️⃣ Pass/Fail (70+ to pass):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Result:   }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{pass\_fail}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# 2) Get indices (and values) of high scorers}
\NormalTok{high\_idx }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.where(scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{85}\NormalTok{)[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{high\_vals }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ scores[high\_idx]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{2️⃣ High Scorers (\textgreater{}85):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Indices: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{high\_idx}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Values : }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{high\_vals}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
==================================================
📊 USING np.where()
==================================================

1️⃣ Pass/Fail (70+ to pass):
Original: [95 87 76 63 89 92 45 78 85 91]
Result:   [95 87 76  0 89 92  0 78 85 91]

2️⃣ High Scorers (>85):
Indices: [0 1 4 5 9]
Values : [95 87 89 92 91]
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Conditional replacement with different values (letter grades)}
\NormalTok{letter\_grades }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.where(scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{90}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
\NormalTok{                np.where(scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{80}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}B\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
\NormalTok{                np.where(scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{70}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}C\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,}
\NormalTok{                np.where(scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}D\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}F\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{))))}

\CommentTok{\# Example 3: Using np.where to find indices}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{3️⃣ Indices of A\textquotesingle{}s and F\textquotesingle{}s:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{a\_idx }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.where(letter\_grades }\OperatorTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{f\_idx }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.where(letter\_grades }\OperatorTok{==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}F\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"A indices: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{a\_idx}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"F indices: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{f\_idx}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}

3️⃣ Indices of A's and F's:
A indices: [0 5 9]
F indices: [6]
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{np.select}: Multi-way Conditional
Logic}{np.select: Multi-way Conditional Logic}}\label{np.select-multi-way-conditional-logic}

While you can nest multiple \texttt{np.where()} calls for complex
conditions, \textbf{\texttt{np.select()}} is preferred for \textbf{3+
branches} because it's more readable and maintainable.

\subsection{Syntax}\label{syntax}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{np.select(conditions, choices, default}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{...)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{conditions}: list of boolean arrays (must be same shape or
  broadcastable)
\item
  \texttt{choices}: list of result values/arrays (same length as
  \texttt{conditions})
\item
  \texttt{default}: value used where no condition is \texttt{True}
  (optional)
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{Example 1 --- Letter grades (cleaner than
nested
\texttt{np.where()})}{Example 1 --- Letter grades (cleaner than nested np.where())}}\label{example-1-letter-grades-cleaner-than-nested-np.where}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{scores }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{95}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{87}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{76}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{63}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{89}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{92}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{45}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{78}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{85}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{91}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{conds   }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{90}\NormalTok{, scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{80}\NormalTok{, scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{70}\NormalTok{, scores }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{choices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}A\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,          }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}B\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,          }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}C\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,          }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}D\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{grades  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.select(conds, choices, default}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}F\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{4️⃣ Letter Grades with np.select():"}\NormalTok{, grades)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original Scores: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}

4️⃣ Letter Grades with np.select(): ['A' 'B' 'C' 'D' 'B' 'A' 'F' 'C' 'B' 'A']
Original Scores: [95 87 76 63 89 92 45 78 85 91]
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Example 2 --- Numeric binning
(labels)}\label{example-2-numeric-binning-labels}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]

\NormalTok{x }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{33}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{47}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{conds }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, (x }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{), x }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{choices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}low\_precision\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}mid\_precision\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}high\_precision\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{buckets }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.select(conds, choices, default}\OperatorTok{=}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}unknown\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# ← Add this!}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(buckets)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
['low_precision' 'mid_precision' 'mid_precision' 'high_precision'
 'high_precision']
\end{verbatim}

\textbf{⚠️ \texttt{np.select} and the \texttt{default} dtype gotcha}

If you omit \texttt{default=...} in \texttt{np.select}, NumPy uses
\textbf{\texttt{0}} as the fallback.\\
When your \texttt{choices} are \textbf{strings}, mixing them with the
integer \texttt{0} forces a common dtype---strings and integers have no
shared dtype---so NumPy raises a \texttt{TypeError}.

\textbf{Example (raises error)}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ numpy }\ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ np}

\NormalTok{x }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{conds   }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, (x }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (x }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{)]}
\NormalTok{choices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}low\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}mid\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}

\NormalTok{np.select(conds, choices)   }\CommentTok{\# default is 0 {-}\textgreater{} TypeError (mixed str + int)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\textbf{Best Practices:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Use \texttt{np.where()}} for simple binary conditions
\item
  \textbf{Use \texttt{np.select()}} for 3+ conditions or complex logic
\item
  \textbf{Always provide a default} to handle edge cases
\item
  \textbf{Test conditions} to ensure they're mutually exclusive when
  needed
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Finding Extremes with \texttt{np.argmin()}
and
\texttt{np.argmax()}}{Finding Extremes with np.argmin() and np.argmax()}}\label{finding-extremes-with-np.argmin-and-np.argmax}

Use these to get the \textbf{index position(s)} of the minimum/maximum
value.\\
Specify an \texttt{axis} for row/column results; omit it for the global
position.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{a }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{i\_min }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.argmin(a)   }\CommentTok{\# 1}
\NormalTok{i\_max }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.argmax(a)   }\CommentTok{\# 2}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"min @ index"}\NormalTok{, i\_min, }\StringTok{"value:"}\NormalTok{, a[i\_min]) }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"max @ index"}\NormalTok{, i\_max, }\StringTok{"value:"}\NormalTok{, a[i\_max])  }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
min @ index 1 value: 1
max @ index 2 value: 9
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]

\CommentTok{\# Create a 2D array (e.g., student test scores)}
\NormalTok{scores }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}
\NormalTok{    [}\DecValTok{85}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{92}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{78}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{95}\NormalTok{],  }\CommentTok{\# Student 0}
\NormalTok{    [}\DecValTok{88}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{76}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{91}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{82}\NormalTok{],  }\CommentTok{\# Student 1}
\NormalTok{    [}\DecValTok{95}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{89}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{84}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{90}\NormalTok{],  }\CommentTok{\# Student 2}
\NormalTok{    [}\DecValTok{72}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{85}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{79}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{88}\NormalTok{]   }\CommentTok{\# Student 3}
\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 Student Test Scores (4 students × 4 tests):"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(scores)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# ============================================}
\CommentTok{\# 1️⃣ FLATTENED (no axis) {-} Returns single index}
\CommentTok{\# ============================================}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"1️⃣ FLATTENED VIEW (axis=None) {-} Single Index"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{min\_idx }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.argmin(scores)}
\NormalTok{max\_idx }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.argmax(scores)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Lowest score index (flattened):  }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{min\_idx}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Highest score index (flattened): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{max\_idx}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Convert flat index to 2D coordinates}
\NormalTok{min\_row, min\_col }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.unravel\_index(min\_idx, scores.shape)}
\NormalTok{max\_row, max\_col }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.unravel\_index(max\_idx, scores.shape)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{🔻 Minimum: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores[min\_row, min\_col]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ at position (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{min\_row}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{min\_col}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   → Student }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{min\_row}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Test }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{min\_col}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"🔺 Maximum: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores[max\_row, max\_col]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ at position (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{max\_row}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{max\_col}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"   → Student }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{max\_row}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Test }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{max\_col}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
📊 Student Test Scores (4 students × 4 tests):
[[85 92 78 95]
 [88 76 91 82]
 [95 89 84 90]
 [72 85 79 88]]

============================================================
1️⃣ FLATTENED VIEW (axis=None) - Single Index
============================================================
Lowest score index (flattened):  12
Highest score index (flattened): 3

🔻 Minimum: 72 at position (3, 0)
   → Student 3, Test 0
🔺 Maximum: 95 at position (0, 3)
   → Student 0, Test 3

============================================================
2️⃣ AXIS=0 (down columns) - Which STUDENT performed best/worst?
============================================================
Lowest scoring student per test:  [3 1 0 1]
Highest scoring student per test: [2 0 1 0]

Detailed breakdown:
  Test 0: Worst = Student 3 (72), Best = Student 2 (95)
  Test 1: Worst = Student 1 (76), Best = Student 0 (92)
  Test 2: Worst = Student 0 (78), Best = Student 1 (91)
  Test 3: Worst = Student 1 (82), Best = Student 0 (95)

============================================================
3️⃣ AXIS=1 (across rows) - Which TEST was easiest/hardest?
============================================================
Worst test per student:  [2 1 2 0]
Best test per student:   [3 2 0 3]

  Student 1: Worst = Test 1 (76), Best = Test 2 (91)
  Student 2: Worst = Test 2 (84), Best = Test 0 (95)
  Student 3: Worst = Test 0 (72), Best = Test 3 (88)
\end{verbatim}

\NormalTok{    worst\_test }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ min\_test\_per\_student[student\_num]}

============================================================
Lowest scoring student per test:  [3 1 0 1]
Highest scoring student per test: [2 0 1 0]

Detailed breakdown:
  Test 0: Worst = Student 3 (72), Best = Student 2 (95)
  Test 1: Worst = Student 1 (76), Best = Student 0 (92)
