\subsection{Advanced Concatenation
Techniques}\label{advanced-concatenation-techniques}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 🚀 ADVANCED TECHNIQUES}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"⚡ PERFORMANCE \& MEMORY OPTIMIZATION"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Performance comparison for large arrays}
\NormalTok{large\_arrays }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [np.random.rand(}\DecValTok{1000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{) }\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ \_ }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{)]}

\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ time}

\CommentTok{\# Method 1: Multiple concatenate calls (inefficient)}
\NormalTok{start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter()}
\NormalTok{result\_slow }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ large\_arrays[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ arr }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ large\_arrays[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{:]:}
\NormalTok{    result\_slow }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.concatenate((result\_slow, arr), axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{slow\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}

\CommentTok{\# Method 2: Single concatenate call (efficient)}
\NormalTok{start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter()}
\NormalTok{result\_fast }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.concatenate(large\_arrays, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{fast\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f" Sequential concatenation: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{slow\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ seconds"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f" Batch concatenation: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{fast\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ seconds"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f" Speedup: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{slow\_time}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{fast\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{x faster"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f" Result shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result\_fast}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f" Memory usage: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result\_fast}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{nbytes }\OperatorTok{/} \FloatTok{1e6}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ MB"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Memory efficiency demonstration}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{💾 MEMORY EFFICIENCY"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{25}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Pre{-}allocate vs concatenate}
\NormalTok{data\_size }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (}\DecValTok{5000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{total\_arrays }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{20}

\CommentTok{\# Method 1: Concatenation (creates multiple copies)}
\NormalTok{start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter()}
\NormalTok{concat\_list }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(total\_arrays):}
\NormalTok{    concat\_list.append(np.random.rand(}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{data\_size))}
\NormalTok{concat\_result }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.concatenate(concat\_list, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{concat\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}

\CommentTok{\# Method 2: Pre{-}allocation (more memory efficient)}
\NormalTok{start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter()}
\NormalTok{preallocated }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.empty((total\_arrays }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ data\_size[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{], data\_size[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]))}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(total\_arrays):}
\NormalTok{    start\_idx }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ data\_size[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{    end\_idx }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (i }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ data\_size[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{    preallocated[start\_idx:end\_idx] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.rand(}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{data\_size)}
\NormalTok{prealloc\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.perf\_counter() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Concatenation method: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{concat\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ seconds"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Pre{-}allocation method: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{prealloc\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{ seconds"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Pre{-}allocation is }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{concat\_time}\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{prealloc\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{x faster"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
⚡ PERFORMANCE & MEMORY OPTIMIZATION
========================================
 Sequential concatenation: 0.0135 seconds
 Batch concatenation: 0.0022 seconds
 Speedup: 6.1x faster
 Result shape: (10000, 100)
 Memory usage: 8.0 MB

💾 MEMORY EFFICIENCY
-------------------------
Concatenation method: 0.0755 seconds
Pre-allocation method: 0.0809 seconds
Pre-allocation is 0.9x faster
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Real-world Application: Time Series
Data}\label{real-world-application-time-series-data}

Let's see concatenation in action with a practical time series example:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\#  TIME SERIES CONCATENATION EXAMPLE}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📊 FINANCIAL DATA PROCESSING"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{35}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Simulate daily stock prices for different months}
\NormalTok{np.random.seed(}\DecValTok{42}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{jan\_prices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.uniform(}\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{120}\NormalTok{, (}\DecValTok{31}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{))  }\CommentTok{\# 31 days, 4 stocks}
\NormalTok{feb\_prices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.uniform(}\DecValTok{98}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{118}\NormalTok{, (}\DecValTok{28}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{))   }\CommentTok{\# 28 days, 4 stocks  }
\NormalTok{mar\_prices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.uniform(}\DecValTok{102}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{122}\NormalTok{, (}\DecValTok{31}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{))  }\CommentTok{\# 31 days, 4 stocks}

\NormalTok{stock\_names }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}AAPL\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}GOOGL\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}MSFT\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}TSLA\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Stock data shape {-} Days × Stocks:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"January: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{jan\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{jan\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ days)"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"February: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{feb\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{feb\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ days)"}\NormalTok{)  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"March: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{mar\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{mar\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ days)"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Combine quarterly data}
\NormalTok{q1\_prices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.concatenate((jan\_prices, feb\_prices, mar\_prices), axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Q1 Combined: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{q1\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{q1\_prices}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ total days)"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Calculate monthly averages}
\NormalTok{monthly\_avg }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}
\NormalTok{    np.mean(jan\_prices, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{),}
\NormalTok{    np.mean(feb\_prices, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{),  }
\NormalTok{    np.mean(mar\_prices, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Monthly averages shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{monthly\_avg}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Monthly averages:"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{months }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}January\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}February\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}March\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i, month }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{enumerate}\NormalTok{(months):}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{month}\SpecialCharTok{:8\}}\SpecialStringTok{: "} \OperatorTok{+} \StringTok{" | "}\NormalTok{.join([}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{stock}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: $}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{avg}\SpecialCharTok{:.2f\}}\SpecialStringTok{"} 
                                      \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ stock, avg }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{zip}\NormalTok{(stock\_names, monthly\_avg[i])]))}

\CommentTok{\# Add new features (volume data) using horizontal concatenation}
\NormalTok{np.random.seed(}\DecValTok{42}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{q1\_volumes }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.randint(}\DecValTok{1000000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5000000}\NormalTok{, (q1\_prices.shape[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{], }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{))}
\NormalTok{q1\_complete }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.hstack((q1\_prices, q1\_volumes))}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{With volume data: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{q1\_complete}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Columns: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{stock\_names}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (prices) + }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{stock\_names}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{ (volumes)"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Sample day 1: Prices=}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{q1\_complete[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, :}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"             Volumes=}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{q1\_complete[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{:]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{astype(}\BuiltInTok{int}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Best Practices}\label{best-practices}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Pre-allocate when possible} for better memory efficiency
\item
  \textbf{Use batch concatenation} instead of iterative concatenation\\
\item
  \textbf{Choose descriptive functions}
  (\texttt{vstack}/\texttt{hstack}) over generic \texttt{concatenate}
  when appropriate
\item
  \textbf{Check shapes first} with \texttt{.shape} to avoid runtime
  errors
\item
  \textbf{Consider memory usage} for large datasets - sometimes lists
  are better for building, then concatenate once
\end{enumerate}

Task 1: Use NumPy to print the name and coordinates of the capital city
closest to the US capital - Washington DC.

\begin{enumerate}

  The \emph{Country Name} for US is given as \emph{United States of

\begin{enumerate}

  Use the \emph{to\_numpy()} function of the \emph{Pandas DataFrame}
  class to convert a DataFrame to a Numpy array
\item
  Use \emph{broadcasting} to compute the euclidean distance of capital
  cities from Washington DC.
\item
  Use \texttt{np.argmin} to locate the index of the minimum value in an
  array
\item
  Exclude the capital itself to avoid trivial zero values in the
  results.
\end{enumerate}

Task 2: Use NumPy to:

  10 cities.

\section{Vectorization in NumPy}\label{vectorization-in-numpy}

\subsection{Introduction to
Vectorization}\label{introduction-to-vectorization}

Vectorization is the process of applying operations to entire arrays or
matrices simultaneously rather than iterating over individual elements
using loops. This approach allows NumPy to utilize highly optimized C
libraries for faster computation.

\pandocbounded{\includegraphics[keepaspectratio]{index_files/mediabag/images-q=tbn-ANd9GcT.png}}

Benefits of Vectorization:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Performance}: Significantly faster than using for-loops in
  Python (often 10-100x speedup)
\item
  \textbf{Conciseness}: Shorter and more readable code
\item
  \textbf{Efficiency}: Reduces the overhead of Python loops and
  leverages lower-level optimizations
\item
  \textbf{Parallelization}: Many vectorized operations can utilize
  multiple CPU cores
\item
  \textbf{Memory Efficiency}: Better cache utilization and reduced
  memory overhead
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Why Vectorization Matters}\label{why-vectorization-matters}

\textbf{Traditional Python Loop Approach:}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Slow: Python loop with individual operations}
\NormalTok{result }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(array1)):}
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ j }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(array2)):}
\NormalTok{        result.append(array1[i] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ array2[j] }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ some\_value)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\textbf{Vectorized NumPy Approach:}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Fast: Single vectorized operation}
\NormalTok{result }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ array1[:, np.newaxis] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ array2 }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ some\_value}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The vectorized approach is faster because: 1. \textbf{Compiled C code}:
NumPy operations use optimized C/Fortran libraries 2. \textbf{Reduced
Python overhead}: Fewer Python function calls and type checks 3.
\textbf{SIMD instructions}: Can use Single Instruction, Multiple Data
operations 4. \textbf{Better memory access patterns}: More
cache-friendly data access

\subsection{Understanding Vectorized Operations with
Examples}\label{understanding-vectorized-operations-with-examples}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]

\CommentTok{\# Create two arrays}
\NormalTok{arr1 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{])}
\NormalTok{arr2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{])}

\CommentTok{\# Element{-}wise addition (vectorized operation)}
\NormalTok{sum\_arr }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ arr1 }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ arr2}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Sum Array:"}\NormalTok{, sum\_arr)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Sum Array: [11 22 33 44 55]
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Types of Vectorized
Operations}\label{types-of-vectorized-operations}

NumPy supports several categories of vectorized operations:

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{1. \textbf{Element-wise Operations
(Universal Functions -
ufuncs)}}{1. Element-wise Operations (Universal Functions - ufuncs)}}\label{element-wise-operations-universal-functions---ufuncs}

These operations apply a function to each element of an array:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Basic arithmetic operations (all vectorized)}
\NormalTok{arr }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{16}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{25}\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Original array:"}\NormalTok{, arr)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Square root:"}\NormalTok{, np.sqrt(arr))}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Natural log:"}\NormalTok{, np.log(arr))}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Sine:"}\NormalTok{, np.sin(arr))}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Power of 2:"}\NormalTok{, np.power(arr, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{))}

\CommentTok{\# Comparison operations}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{Comparison operations:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Greater than 10:"}\NormalTok{, arr }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Equal to 9:"}\NormalTok{, arr }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Between 5 and 20:"}\NormalTok{, (arr }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=} \DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (arr }\OperatorTok{\textless{}=} \DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Original array: [ 1  4  9 16 25]
Square root: [1. 2. 3. 4. 5.]
Natural log: [0.         1.38629436 2.19722458 2.77258872 3.21887582]
Sine: [ 0.84147098 -0.7568025   0.41211849 -0.28790332 -0.13235175]
Power of 2: [  1  16  81 256 625]

Comparison operations:
Greater than 10: [False False False  True  True]
Equal to 9: [False False  True False False]
Between 5 and 20: [False False  True  True False]
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{2. \textbf{Aggregation
Operations}}{2. Aggregation Operations}}\label{aggregation-operations}

These reduce arrays to scalar values or smaller arrays:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# 2D array for aggregation examples}
\NormalTok{matrix }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{],}
\NormalTok{                   [}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{],}
\NormalTok{                   [}\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{11}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{]])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Matrix:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(matrix)}

\CommentTok{\# Aggregations across entire array}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Sum of all elements: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(matrix)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Mean: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{mean(matrix)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Standard deviation: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{std(matrix)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Min: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{min}\NormalTok{(matrix)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Max: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{(matrix)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Aggregations along specific axes}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Sum along axis 0 (columns): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(matrix, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Sum along axis 1 (rows): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(matrix, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Mean along axis 0: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{mean(matrix, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Max along axis 1: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{(matrix, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{3. \textbf{Boolean Operations and Fancy
Indexing}}{3. Boolean Operations and Fancy Indexing}}\label{boolean-operations-and-fancy-indexing}

Vectorized selection and filtering operations:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Boolean indexing {-} vectorized filtering}
\NormalTok{data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{15}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{23}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{16}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{42}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{19}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{])}

\CommentTok{\# Find elements meeting multiple conditions (vectorized)}
\NormalTok{mask }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (data }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{\&}\NormalTok{ (data }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{filtered\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ data[mask]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original data: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{data}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Elements between 5 and 20: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{filtered\_data}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Using np.where for conditional replacement (vectorized)}
\CommentTok{\# Replace values \textgreater{} 15 with {-}1, others with original value}
\NormalTok{result }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.where(data }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{15}\NormalTok{, }\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, data)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"After conditional replacement: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Fancy indexing {-} select multiple elements at once}
\NormalTok{indices }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{selected }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ data[indices]}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Elements at indices }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{indices}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{selected}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Count how many elements meet condition (vectorized)}
\NormalTok{count\_large }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.}\BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(data }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Count of elements \textgreater{} 10: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{count\_large}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Original data: [ 1 15  8 23  4 16 42  3 19  7]
Elements between 5 and 20: [15  8 16 19  7]
After conditional replacement: [ 1 15  8 -1  4 -1 -1  3 -1  7]
Elements at indices [0, 2, 4, 7]: [1 8 4 3]
Count of elements > 10: 5
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{Performance Comparison: NumPy Vectorization Vs Python
Loops}\label{performance-comparison-numpy-vectorization-vs-python-loops}

Understanding the performance benefits of vectorization is crucial for
writing efficient scientific computing code. Let's compare different
scenarios to see when and why vectorization matters.

\subsubsection{Scenario 1: Basic Mathematical
Operations}\label{scenario-1-basic-mathematical-operations}

\texttt{np.dot} is a vectorized operation in NumPy that performs matrix
multiplication or dot product between arrays. It efficiently computes
the element-wise multiplications and then sums them up. To better
understand its efficiency, let's first implement the dot product using
for loops, and then compare its performance with \texttt{np.dot} to see
the benefits of vectorization.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ time}

\CommentTok{\# Function to calculate dot product using for loops}
\KeywordTok{def}\NormalTok{ dot\_product\_loops(arr1, arr2):}
\NormalTok{    result }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(arr1)):}
\NormalTok{        result }\OperatorTok{+=}\NormalTok{ arr1[i] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ arr2[i]}
    \ControlFlowTok{return}\NormalTok{ result}

\CommentTok{\# Create sample arrays of different sizes for comparison}
\NormalTok{sizes }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{1000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{10000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{100000}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1000000}\NormalTok{]}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Performance Comparison: Loops vs NumPy Vectorization"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{60}\NormalTok{)}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ size }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ sizes:}
    \CommentTok{\# Create random arrays}
\NormalTok{    arr1 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.rand(size)}
\NormalTok{    arr2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.rand(size)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Measure time for the loop{-}based implementation}
\NormalTok{    start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()}
\NormalTok{    loop\_result }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ dot\_product\_loops(arr1, arr2)}
\NormalTok{    loop\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Measure time for np.dot}
\NormalTok{    start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()}
\NormalTok{    numpy\_result }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.dot(arr1, arr2)}
\NormalTok{    numpy\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Calculate speedup}
\NormalTok{    speedup }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ loop\_time }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ numpy\_time }\ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ numpy\_time }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0} \ControlFlowTok{else} \BuiltInTok{float}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}inf\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
    
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Array size: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{size}\SpecialCharTok{:,\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Loop result: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{loop\_result}\SpecialCharTok{:.5f\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Time: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{loop\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.5f\}}\SpecialStringTok{s"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"NumPy result: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{numpy\_result}\SpecialCharTok{:.5f\}}\SpecialStringTok{, Time: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{numpy\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.5f\}}\SpecialStringTok{s"}\NormalTok{)}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Speedup: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{speedup}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{x faster"}\NormalTok{)}
    
    

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}=\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{60}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Key Observations:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• NumPy becomes dramatically faster as array size increases"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• Speedup can reach 50{-}100x for large arrays"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"• NumPy overhead is minimal for small arrays but pays off quickly"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Performance Comparison: Loops vs NumPy Vectorization
============================================================

Array size: 1,000
Loop result: 234.28341, Time: 0.00000s
NumPy result: 234.28341, Time: 0.00000s
Speedup: infx faster

Array size: 10,000
Loop result: 2524.58396, Time: 0.00000s
NumPy result: 2524.58396, Time: 0.02460s
Speedup: 0.0x faster

Array size: 100,000
Loop result: 24892.29841, Time: 0.02218s
NumPy result: 24892.29841, Time: 0.00104s
Speedup: 21.4x faster

Array size: 1,000,000
Loop result: 249763.97969, Time: 0.20611s
NumPy result: 249763.97969, Time: 0.00111s
Speedup: 185.6x faster

============================================================
Key Observations:
• NumPy becomes dramatically faster as array size increases
• Speedup can reach 50-100x for large arrays
• NumPy overhead is minimal for small arrays but pays off quickly
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Scenario 2: Complex Mathematical
Operations}\label{scenario-2-complex-mathematical-operations}

Let's compare more complex operations that show even greater performance
differences:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Complex mathematical operation: polynomial evaluation}
\CommentTok{\# f(x) = 3x³ + 2x² {-} 5x + 1}

\KeywordTok{def}\NormalTok{ polynomial\_loops(x\_values):}
    \CommentTok{"""Evaluate polynomial using loops"""}
\NormalTok{    results }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ x }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ x\_values:}
\NormalTok{        result }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{x}\OperatorTok{**}\DecValTok{3} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{x}\OperatorTok{**}\DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{{-}} \DecValTok{5}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{x }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}
\NormalTok{        results.append(result)}
    \ControlFlowTok{return}\NormalTok{ results}

\KeywordTok{def}\NormalTok{ polynomial\_vectorized(x\_values):}
    \CommentTok{"""Evaluate polynomial using vectorized operations"""}
    \ControlFlowTok{return} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{x\_values}\OperatorTok{**}\DecValTok{3} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{x\_values}\OperatorTok{**}\DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{{-}} \DecValTok{5}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{x\_values }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}

\CommentTok{\# Test with different sizes}
\NormalTok{size }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{500000}
\NormalTok{x\_data }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.uniform(}\OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, size)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Complex Operations: Polynomial Evaluation"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"f(x) = 3x³ + 2x² {-} 5x + 1"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Loop version}
\NormalTok{start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()}
\NormalTok{loop\_results }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ polynomial\_loops(x\_data)}
\NormalTok{loop\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}

\CommentTok{\# Vectorized version}
\NormalTok{start\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time()}
\NormalTok{vector\_results }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ polynomial\_vectorized(x\_data)}
\NormalTok{vector\_time }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ time.time() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start\_time}

\NormalTok{speedup }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ loop\_time }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ vector\_time}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Array size: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{size}\SpecialCharTok{:,\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Loop time: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{loop\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{s"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Vectorized time: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{vector\_time}\SpecialCharTok{:.4f\}}\SpecialStringTok{s"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Speedup: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{speedup}\SpecialCharTok{:.1f\}}\SpecialStringTok{x"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Verify results match}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Results match: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{allclose(loop\_results, vector\_results)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Complex Operations: Polynomial Evaluation
f(x) = 3x³ + 2x² - 5x + 1
----------------------------------------
Array size: 500,000
Loop time: 0.2560s
Vectorized time: 0.0129s
Speedup: 19.9x
Results match: True
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Performance Summary \& Key
Takeaways}\label{performance-summary-key-takeaways}

The performance comparisons clearly demonstrate that \textbf{vectorized
NumPy operations significantly outperform equivalent Python loops}:

\subsection{Broadcasting: The Heart of NumPy
Vectorization}\label{broadcasting-the-heart-of-numpy-vectorization}

Broadcasting is NumPy's powerful mechanism that allows operations
between arrays of different shapes without explicitly reshaping them.
It's the foundation that makes vectorization so flexible and intuitive.

\subsubsection{Broadcasting Rules}\label{broadcasting-rules}

NumPy broadcasting follows these rules:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Start from the trailing dimension} and work backwards
\item
  \textbf{Dimensions are compatible} if:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    They are equal, OR
  \item
    One of them is 1, OR\\
  \item
    One of them doesn't exist (missing dimension)
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Missing dimensions} are assumed to be size 1
\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Visual Guide to
Broadcasting}\label{visual-guide-to-broadcasting}

\begin{verbatim}
Array 1: (3, 4)     [[1, 2, 3, 4],      Array 2: (4,)    [10, 20, 30, 40]
                     [5, 6, 7, 8],                         ↓ broadcasts to
                     [9,10,11,12]]                         [[10, 20, 30, 40],
                                                            [10, 20, 30, 40], 
                                                            [10, 20, 30, 40]]
Result: (3, 4)      Element-wise addition produces (3, 4) result
\end{verbatim}

Let's explore different broadcasting scenarios:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Comprehensive Broadcasting Examples}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"=== BROADCASTING EXAMPLES ===}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Example 1: 2D array + 1D array (most common case)}
\NormalTok{arr\_2d }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                   [}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                   [}\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{11}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{]])}

\NormalTok{arr\_1d }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{20}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{])}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Example 1: (3,4) + (4,) broadcasting"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"2D array shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{arr\_2d}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"1D array shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{arr\_1d}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{result\_1 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ arr\_2d }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ arr\_1d}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Result shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result\_1}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Result:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(result\_1)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# Example 2: Broadcasting with different orientations}
\NormalTok{arr\_col }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                    [}\DecValTok{200}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                    [}\DecValTok{300}\NormalTok{]])  }\CommentTok{\# Column vector (3,1)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Example 2: (3,4) + (3,1) broadcasting"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"2D array shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{arr\_2d}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Column vector shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{arr\_col}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{result\_2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ arr\_2d }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ arr\_col}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Result shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result\_2}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Result:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(result\_2)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# Example 3: Scalar broadcasting (always works)}
\NormalTok{scalar }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{1000}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Example 3: (3,4) + scalar broadcasting"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{result\_3 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ arr\_2d }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ scalar}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Result shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result\_3}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Result:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(result\_3)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# Example 4: 3D broadcasting}
\NormalTok{arr\_3d }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.randint(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{, (}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{))}
\NormalTok{arr\_2d\_broadcast }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]])  }\CommentTok{\# (1, 4)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Example 4: (2,3,4) + (1,4) broadcasting"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"3D array shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{arr\_3d}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"2D array shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{arr\_2d\_broadcast}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{result\_4 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ arr\_3d }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ arr\_2d\_broadcast}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Result shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{result\_4}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Broadcasting successful!"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
=== BROADCASTING EXAMPLES ===

Example 1: (3,4) + (4,) broadcasting
2D array shape: (3, 4)
1D array shape: (4,)
Result shape: (3, 4)
Result:
[[11 22 33 44]
 [15 26 37 48]
 [19 30 41 52]]

Example 2: (3,4) + (3,1) broadcasting
2D array shape: (3, 4)
Column vector shape: (3, 1)
Result shape: (3, 4)
Result:
[[101 102 103 104]
 [205 206 207 208]
 [309 310 311 312]]

Example 3: (3,4) + scalar broadcasting
Result shape: (3, 4)
Result:
[[1001 1002 1003 1004]
 [1005 1006 1007 1008]
 [1009 1010 1011 1012]]

Example 4: (2,3,4) + (1,4) broadcasting
3D array shape: (2, 3, 4)
2D array shape: (1, 4)
Result shape: (2, 3, 4)
Broadcasting successful!
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Broadcasting Rules Demonstration}

\KeywordTok{def}\NormalTok{ check\_broadcast\_compatibility(shape1, shape2):}
    \CommentTok{"""}
\CommentTok{    Check if two shapes are compatible for broadcasting}
\CommentTok{    """}
    \CommentTok{\# Pad shorter shape with 1s on the left}
\NormalTok{    ndim1, ndim2 }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(shape1), }\BuiltInTok{len}\NormalTok{(shape2)}
\NormalTok{    max\_ndim }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{max}\NormalTok{(ndim1, ndim2)}
    
\NormalTok{    shape1\_padded }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ (max\_ndim }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ ndim1) }\OperatorTok{+} \BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(shape1)}
\NormalTok{    shape2\_padded }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ (max\_ndim }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ ndim2) }\OperatorTok{+} \BuiltInTok{list}\NormalTok{(shape2)}
    
\NormalTok{    result\_shape }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}
\NormalTok{    compatible }\OperatorTok{=} \VariableTok{True}
    
    \ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(max\_ndim):}
\NormalTok{        dim1, dim2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ shape1\_padded[i], shape2\_padded[i]}
        \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ dim1 }\OperatorTok{==}\NormalTok{ dim2:}
\NormalTok{            result\_shape.append(dim1)}
        \ControlFlowTok{elif}\NormalTok{ dim1 }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{            result\_shape.append(dim2)}
        \ControlFlowTok{elif}\NormalTok{ dim2 }\OperatorTok{==} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{            result\_shape.append(dim1)}
        \ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{:}
\NormalTok{            compatible }\OperatorTok{=} \VariableTok{False}
            \ControlFlowTok{break}
    
    \ControlFlowTok{return}\NormalTok{ compatible, }\BuiltInTok{tuple}\NormalTok{(result\_shape) }\ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ compatible }\ControlFlowTok{else} \VariableTok{None}

\CommentTok{\# Test different shape combinations}
\NormalTok{test\_cases }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{    ((}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{), (}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{,)),      }\CommentTok{\# Compatible}
\NormalTok{    ((}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{), (}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)),    }\CommentTok{\# Compatible  }
\NormalTok{    ((}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{), (}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{,)),      }\CommentTok{\# Incompatible}
\NormalTok{    ((}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{), (}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{,)),   }\CommentTok{\# Compatible}
\NormalTok{    ((}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{), (}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{)), }\CommentTok{\# Compatible}
\NormalTok{    ((}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{), (}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{)), }\CommentTok{\# Compatible}
\NormalTok{    ((}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{), (}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{)),    }\CommentTok{\# Incompatible}
\NormalTok{]}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Broadcasting Compatibility Check:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}"} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ shape1, shape2 }\KeywordTok{in}\NormalTok{ test\_cases:}
\NormalTok{    compatible, result\_shape }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ check\_broadcast\_compatibility(shape1, shape2)}
\NormalTok{    status }\OperatorTok{=} \StringTok{"✅ Compatible"} \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ compatible }\ControlFlowTok{else} \StringTok{"❌ Incompatible"}
    \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ compatible:}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{str}\NormalTok{(shape1)}\SpecialCharTok{:\textgreater{}10\}}\SpecialStringTok{ + }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{str}\NormalTok{(shape2)}\SpecialCharTok{:\textgreater{}10\}}\SpecialStringTok{ → }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{str}\NormalTok{(result\_shape)}\SpecialCharTok{:\textgreater{}12\}}\SpecialStringTok{ }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{status}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
    \ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{:}
        \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{str}\NormalTok{(shape1)}\SpecialCharTok{:\textgreater{}10\}}\SpecialStringTok{ + }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\BuiltInTok{str}\NormalTok{(shape2)}\SpecialCharTok{:\textgreater{}10\}}\SpecialStringTok{ → }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}N/A\textquotesingle{}}\SpecialCharTok{:\textgreater{}12\}}\SpecialStringTok{ }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{status}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Broadcasting Compatibility Check:
--------------------------------------------------
    (3, 4) +       (4,) →       (3, 4) ✅ Compatible
    (3, 4) +     (3, 1) →       (3, 4) ✅ Compatible
    (3, 4) +       (2,) →          N/A ❌ Incompatible
 (2, 3, 4) +       (4,) →    (2, 3, 4) ✅ Compatible
 (2, 3, 4) +     (3, 4) →    (2, 3, 4) ✅ Compatible
 (2, 3, 4) +  (2, 1, 4) →    (2, 3, 4) ✅ Compatible
    (3, 4) +     (2, 3) →          N/A ❌ Incompatible
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{Real-World Broadcasting
Applications}\label{real-world-broadcasting-applications}

Broadcasting enables elegant solutions to common data science problems:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Real{-}world broadcasting applications}

\CommentTok{\# Application 1: Data Normalization (Z{-}score standardization)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"=== APPLICATION 1: DATA NORMALIZATION ==="}\NormalTok{)}
\CommentTok{\# Sample data: test scores for 100 students across 5 subjects}
\NormalTok{np.random.seed(}\DecValTok{42}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{scores }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.normal(}\DecValTok{75}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{15}\NormalTok{, (}\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{))  }\CommentTok{\# 100 students, 5 subjects}
\NormalTok{subjects }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Math\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Science\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}English\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}History\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Art\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original data shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Sample scores (first 5 students):"}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{range}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{):}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Student }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{i}\OperatorTok{+}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{scores[i]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Calculate mean and std for each subject (broadcasting will handle the rest)}
\NormalTok{subject\_means }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.mean(scores, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# Shape: (5,)}
\NormalTok{subject\_stds }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.std(scores, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)    }\CommentTok{\# Shape: (5,)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Subject means: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{subject\_means}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Subject stds: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{subject\_stds}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Normalize using broadcasting: (100,5) {-} (5,) / (5,) → (100,5)}
\NormalTok{normalized\_scores }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (scores }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ subject\_means) }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ subject\_stds}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Normalized data shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{normalized\_scores}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Normalized means (should be \textasciitilde{}0): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{mean(normalized\_scores, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Normalized stds (should be \textasciitilde{}1): }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{np}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{std(normalized\_scores, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# Application 2: Distance Matrix Calculation  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"=== APPLICATION 2: DISTANCE MATRIX ==="}\NormalTok{)}
\CommentTok{\# Calculate pairwise distances between points using broadcasting}
\NormalTok{points }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{], [}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{], [}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{], [}\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{]])  }\CommentTok{\# 4 points in 2D}
\NormalTok{n\_points }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ points.shape[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Points shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{points}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Points:"}\NormalTok{)}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ i, point }\KeywordTok{in} \BuiltInTok{enumerate}\NormalTok{(points):}
    \BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"  Point }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{i}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{: (}\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{point[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{, }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{point[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{)"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Using broadcasting to calculate all pairwise distances efficiently}
\CommentTok{\# points[:, np.newaxis, :] has shape (4, 1, 2)  }
\CommentTok{\# points[np.newaxis, :, :] has shape (1, 4, 2)}
\CommentTok{\# Broadcasting gives us (4, 4, 2) {-} all pairwise differences}
\NormalTok{differences }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ points[:, np.newaxis, :] }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ points[np.newaxis, :, :]}
\NormalTok{distances }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.sqrt(np.}\BuiltInTok{sum}\NormalTok{(differences}\OperatorTok{**}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, axis}\OperatorTok{=}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{))}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Distance matrix shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{distances}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Distance matrix:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(distances.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{))}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# Application 3: Image Processing with Broadcasting}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"=== APPLICATION 3: IMAGE PROCESSING ==="}\NormalTok{)}
\CommentTok{\# Simulate a grayscale image and apply different brightness adjustments to RGB channels}
\NormalTok{np.random.seed(}\DecValTok{42}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{image\_gray }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.random.randint(}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{256}\NormalTok{, (}\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{))  }\CommentTok{\# 100x100 grayscale image}

\CommentTok{\# Create RGB image by broadcasting}
\NormalTok{rgb\_multipliers }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\FloatTok{1.0}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.8}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.6}\NormalTok{])  }\CommentTok{\# R, G, B channel multipliers}
\CommentTok{\# Reshape for broadcasting: (100, 100, 1) * (3,) → (100, 100, 3)}
\NormalTok{image\_rgb }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ image\_gray[:, :, np.newaxis] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ rgb\_multipliers}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original grayscale image shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{image\_gray}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"RGB multipliers: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{rgb\_multipliers}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Final RGB image shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{image\_rgb}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"RGB image dtype: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{image\_rgb}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{dtype}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# Show some pixel values}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Sample pixel transformation:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"Original gray value: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{image\_gray[}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"RGB values: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{image\_rgb[}\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{50}\NormalTok{]}\SpecialCharTok{.}\BuiltInTok{round}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{()}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"💡 Key Broadcasting Benefits:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"  • No explicit loops required"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"  • Memory efficient (no array copying)"}\NormalTok{)  }
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"  • Highly optimized C implementation"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"  • Readable and concise code"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"  • Scales to any dimension"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{arr2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                 [}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                 [}\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]])}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{arr4 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{])}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{arr2 }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ arr4}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
array([[ 5,  7,  9, 11],
       [ 9, 11, 13, 15],
       [13,  6,  8, 10]])
\end{verbatim}

When the expression \texttt{arr2\ +\ arr4} is evaluated, \texttt{arr4}
(which has the shape \texttt{(4,)}) is replicated three times to match
the shape \texttt{(3,\ 4)} of \texttt{arr2}. Numpy performs the
replication without actually creating three copies of the smaller
dimension array, thus improving performance and using lower memory.

Broadcasting only works if one of the arrays can be replicated to match
the other array's shape.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Dimensions of size 1 will broadcast (as if the value was repeated).
\item
  Otherwise, the dimension must have the same shape.
\end{itemize}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{arr5 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([}\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{])}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# uncomment the code to see the error}
\CommentTok{\# arr2 + arr5}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

In the above example, even if \texttt{arr5} is replicated three times,
it will not match the shape of \texttt{arr2}. Hence
\texttt{arr2\ +\ arr5} cannot be evaluated successfully. See the
\href{https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/basics.broadcasting.html}{broadcasting
documentation} to learn more about it.

\subsection{Matrix Multiplication in NumPy with
Vectorization}\label{matrix-multiplication-in-numpy-with-vectorization}

Matrix multiplication is one of the most common and computationally
intensive operations in numerical computing and deep learning. NumPy
offers efficient and highly optimized methods for performing matrix
multiplication, which leverage vectorization to handle large matrices
quickly and accurately.

\textbf{Note that}: NumPy matrix operations follow the standard rules of
linear algebra, so it's important to ensure that the shapes of the
matrices are compatible. If they are not, consider reshaping the
matrices before performing multiplication

There are two commonly methods for matrix multiplication

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{Method 1: Matrix Multiplication Using
\texttt{np.dot()}}{Method 1: Matrix Multiplication Using np.dot()}}\label{method-1-matrix-multiplication-using-np.dot}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Define two 2D arrays (matrices)}
\NormalTok{matrix1 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                    [}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{]])}
\NormalTok{matrix2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.array([[}\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                    [}\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{], }
\NormalTok{                    [}\DecValTok{11}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{]])}

\CommentTok{\# Matrix multiplication using np.dot}
\NormalTok{result\_dot }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.dot(matrix1, matrix2)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Matrix Multiplication using np.dot:}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"}\NormalTok{, result\_dot)}

\CommentTok{\# Another way to perform np.dot for matrix multiplication}
\NormalTok{result\_dot2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ matrix1.dot(matrix2)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{Matrix Multiplication using dot method:}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"}\NormalTok{, result\_dot2)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
Matrix Multiplication using np.dot:
 [[ 58  64]
 [139 154]]

Matrix Multiplication using dot method:
 [[ 58  64]
 [139 154]]
\end{verbatim}

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{Method 2: Matrix Multiplication using
\texttt{np.matmul()} or
\texttt{@}}{Method 2: Matrix Multiplication using np.matmul() or @}}\label{method-2-matrix-multiplication-using-np.matmul-or}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Matrix multiplication using np.matmul or @ operator}
\NormalTok{result\_matmul }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ np.matmul(matrix1, matrix2)}
\NormalTok{result\_operator }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ matrix1 }\OperatorTok{@}\NormalTok{ matrix2}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{Matrix Multiplication using np.matmul:}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"}\NormalTok{, result\_matmul)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{Matrix Multiplication using @ operator:}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"}\NormalTok{, result\_operator)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}

Matrix Multiplication using np.matmul:
 [[ 58  64]
 [139 154]]

Matrix Multiplication using @ operator:
 [[ 58  64]
 [139 154]]
\end{verbatim}

Note that \texttt{*} operator in numpy is element-wise multiplication

\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# using * operator for element{-}wise multiplication, please uncomment the code below to run}
\CommentTok{\# element\_wise = matrix1 * matrix2}
\CommentTok{\# print("\textbackslash{}nElement{-}wise Multiplication:\textbackslash{}n", element\_wise)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# reshape the array for element{-}wise multiplication}
\NormalTok{matrix2\_reshaped }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ matrix2.reshape(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{, }\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{element\_wise }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ matrix1 }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ matrix2\_reshaped}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{Element{-}wise Multiplication after reshaping:}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\StringTok{"}\NormalTok{, element\_wise)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\section{Converting Between NumPy Arrays and Pandas
DataFrames}\label{converting-between-numpy-arrays-and-pandas-dataframes}

\textbf{Seamless data conversion} between NumPy and pandas is essential
for efficient data science workflows. Each library excels in different
areas, and knowing when and how to convert between them maximizes your
analytical power.

\subsection{Why Conversion Matters}\label{why-conversion-matters}

\textbf{NumPy} and \textbf{pandas} complement each other perfectly:

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2308}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3462}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.4231}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
\textbf{Aspect}
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
\textbf{NumPy Arrays}
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
\textbf{Pandas DataFrames}
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Strength} & Mathematical computations & Data manipulation \&
analysis \\
\textbf{Speed} & ⚡ Faster numerical operations & 🔍 Easier data
exploration \\
\textbf{Memory} & 💾 More memory efficient & 🏷️ Rich metadata (labels,
dtypes) \\
\textbf{Use Cases} & Linear algebra, statistics, ML algorithms & Data
cleaning, grouping, merging \\
\textbf{Indexing} & Integer-based only & Label-based + integer-based \\
\textbf{Missing Data} & Limited NaN support & 🛡️ Robust NaN handling \\
\end{longtable}

\textbf{Typical Workflow}: 1. \textbf{Load data} with pandas (CSV,
Excel, databases) 2. \textbf{Clean and prepare} with pandas (filtering,
grouping) 3. \textbf{Convert to NumPy} for intensive computations (ML,
statistics) 4. \textbf{Convert back to pandas} for results analysis and
visualization

\subsection{NumPy Array → Pandas
DataFrame}\label{numpy-array-pandas-dataframe}

\textbf{When to convert}: You have computational results in NumPy arrays
and need pandas' data manipulation capabilities.

\textbf{Common scenarios}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Adding meaningful labels to numerical results
\item
  Exporting to CSV, Excel, or databases
\item
  Preparing data for visualization libraries
\item
  Using pandas' powerful filtering and grouping
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Basic Conversion Methods}\label{basic-conversion-methods}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"🔄 NUMPY TO PANDAS CONVERSION"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"="} \OperatorTok{*} \DecValTok{40}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\textbf{💡 Pro Tips}:- \textbf{Check data types} after conversion with
\texttt{df.dtypes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Always specify meaningful column names} for better code
  readability
\item
  \textbf{Use \texttt{pd.Index()}} to add names to your index/columns
  for richer metadata
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Pandas DataFrame → NumPy
Array}\label{pandas-dataframe-numpy-array}

\textbf{When to convert}: You need NumPy's computational speed and
mathematical functions.

\subsubsection{Conversion Methods \&
Performance}\label{conversion-methods-performance}

\textbf{Common scenarios}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Performance-critical computations (linear algebra, statistics)
\item
  Integration with scientific computing libraries (SciPy, scikit-learn)
\item
  Machine learning algorithms that expect NumPy arrays
\item
  Mathematical operations not available in pandas
\end{itemize}

\begin{Shaded}

        \StringTok{"TSLA"}\NormalTok{:  [}\FloatTok{800.0}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{795.0}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{820.0}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{815.0}\NormalTok{],}
\NormalTok{    \},}
\NormalTok{    index}\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{[}\StringTok{"Day 1"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Day 2"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Day 3"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Day 4"}\NormalTok{]}
\NormalTok{)}

\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"📈 Original DataFrame:"}\NormalTok{)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(stock\_data)}
\BuiltInTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialStringTok{f"}\CharTok{\textbackslash{}n}\SpecialStringTok{Shape: }\SpecialCharTok{\{}\NormalTok{stock\_data}\SpecialCharTok{.}\NormalTok{shape}\SpecialCharTok{\}}\SpecialStringTok{"}\NormalTok{)}
